title: OPERATION WET SEASON
skeleton: occupied farming district's stay-behind cell must make a producing region cost more than its harvest is worth, while its only cover is the civilian census that the enemy's reprisal apparatus turns against the people who shelter it
inspiration: rice-paddy insurgency under census control and collective reprisal — the Mekong Delta hamlet war, 1965
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT} — currently administered by {TARGET_FACTION} occupation forces, {YEAR}. The Barrage is a 3.4-kilometer earthfill dam across the river. It feeds 61,000 hectares of terraced rice paddy that grows 38 percent of the continent's rice, and the occupier needs that rice: the garrison eats from it and ships the surplus offworld in requisition convoys that run the Barrage Crest Road every 6 days. {EMPLOYER} has activated your cell — 23 fighters, 2 salvage-grade light 'Mechs hidden in a flooded quarry, and 4 tons of mixed munitions — with one standing order: make the occupation of {WORLD}'s irrigation district cost the enemy more than the rice is worth, without getting the district burned in reprisal while you do it. The terrain works against you. Below the dam the land is flooded paddy from levee to levee. A BattleMech that steps off a levee crown sinks to the hip — 1.2 meters of water over 2 meters of mud — and is then stuck, unable to move, an easy salvage prize for enemy recovery teams. Only the levee crowns (4 to 6 meters wide, wide enough for single-file movement) and the Crest Road (11 meters, two lanes) will carry a 'Mech, which means every route you can use is a route the garrison can predict and watch. Fourteen sensor pickets cover the road network. That count comes from {NPC:resistance-leader} and is 9 days old, so treat it as a floor. The real cost of this campaign is paid by the local people. Your fighters are registered as levee-maintenance workers — 2,214 names on the occupation's census, re-verified every 12 days by retinal scan at the district administrative compound. The garrison's reprisal policy is published and exact: for each insurgent incident inside the irrigation district, it cuts the nearest work brigade's ration credits in half for 30 days and detains 3 levee captains for interrogation. {NPC:counterintel-hunter} runs the informer network and pays informers in ration credits — which the reprisals make more valuable, so every attack you stage inside the district makes informing on you more attractive. Every attack you stage outside the district instead burns fuel and exposure you cannot replace. Garrison strength: 1 'Mech company (12 machines, a light-medium mix), 1 motorized infantry battalion spread across 6 compounds, and 1 aerospace flight at an airstrip 40 kilometers to the south. That last one is unconfirmed — it is inferred from fuel-truck counts that levee workers reported 11 days ago, so it may not be there at all. The convoys are the weak point: 8 trucks, 2 escort vehicles, and 1 'Mech, running on a schedule the garrison believes is secret. It is not secret to you. The hard part is reading that schedule week after week without the cell being found out. Learning it depends on the census cover, and the census cover is what every attack puts at risk.

objectives.primary: Destroy or turn back 3 requisition convoys within 60 days, and keep the cell's census cover intact so the enemy never identifies its members.
objectives.secondary: Disable 5 of the 14 sensor pickets, leaving no physical evidence that could be traced back to the work brigades.
objectives.bonus: Steal the occupation's biometric census database during a 12-day verification cycle. Without it, the garrison loses the records it uses to pick reprisal targets.

complications.name: Census Resweep
complications.text: After the first incident inside the district, the garrison shortens the verification cycle from 12 days to 8 and adds gait-pattern checks at the compound gate. Fighters who have been carrying ammunition crates walk differently and the scanners are calibrated to notice.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each mission staged inside the irrigation district adds +1 cumulative to the cell's discovery track. At 3, one fighter is flagged for interrogation; at 5, the cell's quarry hide is compromised.

complications.name: Monsoon Crest
complications.text: Nine days of sustained rain raise the reservoir to within 0.4 meters of spillway crest. Levee crowns soften and narrow; the garrison grounds its aerospace flight; the paddy deepens.
complications.mechanicalEffect: While active: levee crowns count one width class narrower for 'Mech movement, visibility caps at 300 meters, aerospace support unavailable to both sides, bog checks worsen by one step.

complications.name: Informer Bounty
complications.text: After the second convoy loss the garrison doubles the informer bounty and pays in protein ration, not scrip. Hungry districts produce reliable witnesses.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any cell action observed by civilians is reported to the garrison within 4-8 hours on a 50 percent roll, rising to 75 percent in brigades currently under ration reprisal.

decisionPoints.name: Where the Cell Sleeps
decisionPoints.context: The verification cycle is tightening and the quarry hide will not survive a saturation sweep. The cell must decide where it lives before the next census window closes.

options.title: Stay in the Census
advantages: Full civilian cover and freedom of movement on work passes
Inside access to the administrative compound and convoy scheduling gossip
disadvantages: Reprisals land on the cell's own families and work brigades
One flagged fighter under interrogation can unravel all 23 names
options.consequence: Future missions roll against the discovery track, but intelligence quality on garrison movements is rated HIGH for the campaign's duration.

costs.resource: discovery track: +1 cumulative per mission staged inside the district
costs.risk: one flagged fighter under interrogation can unravel all 23 names

options.title: Move to the Drowned Monastery
advantages: An island in the reservoir, off-census, unreachable by ground sweep without boats the garrison does not have
Reprisal exposure for the brigades drops to zero for cell-attributed actions
disadvantages: Resupply is 2 night-boat trips per week and weather-dependent
23 names going absent flags the entire roster as fugitives within one verification cycle
options.consequence: The cell survives independent of the district, but the garrison declares the 23 fugitives and relocates their families to the administrative compound as leverage.

costs.resource: resupply drops to 2 night-boat trips per week, weather-dependent
costs.risk: 23 census absences flag the entire roster as fugitives within one 12-day verification cycle

options.title: Split the Cell
advantages: 11 names keep their census cover and the intelligence tap
12 fighters and both 'Mechs operate from the monastery without reprisal linkage
disadvantages: Courier traffic between the halves becomes the new vulnerability
Neither half can independently execute a convoy ambush at full effect
options.consequence: Two half-strength cells with a courier route the enemy can find; if {NPC:counterintel-hunter} intercepts one courier, both halves are mapped.

costs.resource: convoy-ambush capability: neither half can execute one at full effect
costs.risk: one intercepted courier maps both halves of the cell

decisionPoints.name: The Third Convoy
decisionPoints.context: {EMPLOYER} requires a third convoy destroyed before the offworld grain lift departs. Only three options remain: one ambush site inside the district and two outside it. Each one carries a different cost — civilian reprisal, fuel and exposure, or destroying food the district itself needs.

options.title: Crest Road Ambush
advantages: Terrain canalizes the escort onto an 11-meter road with paddy on both flanks
Wreck recovery into the flooded quarry is feasible within 90 minutes
disadvantages: Inside the district: reprisal lands on Work Brigade 4, 312 households
Cratering the Crest Road interrupts irrigation control for an estimated 20 days
options.consequence: Convoy kill is near-certain, but winter rice yield drops and occupation bulletins lay the hunger at the insurgency's door — recruiting falls in the affected brigades.

costs.resource: reprisal bill: Work Brigade 4 (312 households) at half ration credits for 30 days, 3 levee captains detained; irrigation control out an estimated 20 days
costs.risk: winter rice yield falls and the hunger is billed to the insurgency

options.title: Ferry Slip at the Southern Strip
advantages: Outside the irrigation district — no reprisal mechanism applies
Destroys the transfer point, not just one convoy: 6-day schedule slips to 14
disadvantages: 40 kilometers of exposed transit past 5 sensor pickets, each way
The round trip burns 60 percent of the cell's remaining 'Mech fuel
options.consequence: Success leaves the cell's 'Mechs immobile for 17 days pending a fuel purchase from {NPC:smuggler-captain} at his price, on his schedule.

costs.resource: 'Mech fuel: 60 percent of remaining stock — replacement only from {NPC:smuggler-captain} at his price, on his schedule
costs.risk: 80 kilometers of exposed round-trip transit past 5 sensor pickets

options.title: Spoil the Cargo
advantages: No shots fired; a fungal contaminant in the drying yards reads as crop disease
Cell exposure is one work-pass entry by 2 fighters
disadvantages: Destroys food that district civilians also eat through the winter
Verification takes 21 days and {EMPLOYER} may not credit an invisible kill
options.consequence: The grain lift leaves under-loaded and the garrison tightens local rations anyway. The district still goes hungry this winter — from a smaller harvest rather than from a reprisal — and the cell has to decide whether that difference actually mattered.

costs.resource: the district's own winter food margin — civilians eat from the same drying yards
costs.risk: 21-day verification lag; {EMPLOYER} may not credit an invisible kill toward the 3-convoy quota

entries.event: Convoy escort transmits flash contact report; garrison TOC logs the alarm.
QRF lance (4 'Mechs) departs the central compound, 14 kilometers out by road.
Sensor pickets cross-cue; road gates at both district exits close; work passes suspended.
QRF lance reaches the ambush grid; recovery and forensics teams follow at 15-minute trail.
VTOL pair on station, thermal-sweeping the levee net lane by lane.
Infantry cordon closes around the nearest work-brigade hamlet; detentions begin.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: All cell elements must break up into groups of fewer than 4 people by T+0:40. At T+0:40 the VTOL thermal sweep begins. Any 'Mech-sized heat source still moving on a levee crown after that will be located and tracked, the 'Mech will be hunted down and captured, and the cell members and the civilians who sheltered them will be rounded up with it.

opforSketch.composition: Garrison-grade light/medium 'Mech company (12 machines, Regular), motorized infantry battalion (Green, dispersed across 6 compounds), 2 VTOLs, 1 conventional fighter flight at 40 kilometers. Convoy escorts: 1 'Mech, 2 armed trucks. Generator should weight fast light movers with sensor supports over assault tonnage.
opforSketch.behavior: Cordon-and-document doctrine: contain the incident, sweep the area with thermal imagers, then punish through the census system rather than chase the attackers. The garrison takes few combat risks — {NPC:opfor-commander} would rather punish civilians than risk damaging his own machines, and that preference is the single biggest weakness this campaign can exploit.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY POWDER
forks.trigger: Three convoys destroyed or turned and the cell's census cover intact at day 60.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} stages an arms drop at the Drowned Monastery: 2 additional light 'Mechs, 12 tons munitions, and a Maskirovka adviser arriving via {NPC:quest-giver}. The cell graduates to company-scale operations and a district-wide target list.

forks.name: OPERATION TEN HOUSEHOLDS
forks.trigger: Cell cover broken, or 2 or more fighters flagged on the discovery track.
forks.consequence: Detentions reach the cell's families. The mission becomes a 96-hour extraction of 23 fighters and 41 dependents through the paddy net before the compound's transport lift departs — with the informer net awake and paid.

forks.name: OPERATION RICE COUNT
forks.trigger: Convoy quota met but the Crest Road cratered or irrigation control interrupted.
forks.consequence: Winter yield falls 22 percent. {EMPLOYER} orders the cell to start raiding the occupation's own requisition stores to feed the brigade families — the same skills used for a harder job, against a garrison that now expects exactly these raids.

storyElementSeed: A levee captain counts ration chits across a kitchen table, twice, then a third time, while rain works at the shutters; the count does not change, and two of the chits are owed to a family whose names are about to leave the census.

merc.objectives.primary: Contract terms: 3 requisition convoys destroyed or turned back within 60 days. Keeping the cell's cover intact is part of the job, not an optional extra — clause 9 cancels the completion bonus if the cell is rounded up within 30 days of the third convoy.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Ferry Slip at the Southern Strip
resourceGates.lackingText: No depot access: the 60 percent of fuel spent on this option can only be replaced by {NPC:smuggler-captain}, at his price and on his schedule. Treat the resulting 17-day immobilization as the fixed cost of choosing this option.

phases.name: SUSTAINMENT
phases.lead: Between convoy windows the cell is not a military object: it is 23 census entries who maintain levees, draw rations, and pass retinal verification every 12 days. Cover maintenance is the campaign's main effort; the strikes are only what the cover buys.

dataBlock.Verification cycle: every 12 days at the district administrative compound, retinal scan, all 2,214 registered names — shortens to 8 days after the first in-district incident
dataBlock.Quarry hide: 2 light 'Mechs submerged to the canopy in the flooded quarry; reactivation to walking order 50 minutes including seal purge
dataBlock.Munitions: 4 tons mixed; no replacement line except {EMPLOYER} drop or {NPC:smuggler-captain}
dataBlock.Movement writ: levee crews hold work passes for 05:30-19:00; night movement requires a maintenance writ, 14 issued per brigade per month

phases.protocol: Cell signals run through laundry and produce, never radio: a white sleeping mat airing on the Hou compound wall means verification sweep inside 24 hours — scatter the quarry watch; a rice price chalked on the Wei junction market board ending in 8 means the courier meeting is on, ending in 3 means burn the route. Radio exists for one word — the abort signal XIAOSHU, sent in clear, once. Anything longer is direction-found inside 4 minutes.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Which 3 of the 14 sensor pickets the garrison reads in real time versus on tape, and what the informer bounty buys in a brigade already under ration reprisal.

phases.name: STRIKE
phases.lead: A convoy kill is 11 minutes of violence purchased with 6 days of watching. The escort is 1 light 'Mech leading and 2 armed trucks at positions 2 and 9; the killing ground is the 1,400-meter reach of the Crest Road between Spillway 2 and the southern fork, where paddy flanks both shoulders and nothing heavier than a bicycle leaves the road.

routes.name: Route EEL
routes.desc: the Mian east levee maintenance crown, 5 meters wide, single file, screened by windbreak poplars for 2.1 of its 3.0 kilometers
routes.tradeoff: Fastest 'Mech approach to the Crest Road. It passes sensor picket 9, which reports on a 20-minute tape delay. That delay is 9 days old, so plan for it to be shorter.

routes.name: Route CARP
routes.desc: the bund line south of the Barrage, 4 meters wide, 2 fords
routes.tradeoff: No picket coverage anywhere on its length; the crown rates soft after rain, and a misstep is a hip-deep bog the cell cannot recover under fire.

dataBlock.Convoy composition: 8 cargo trucks at 4.5 tons rice each, 2 armed escort trucks, 1 light 'Mech
dataBlock.Interval: every 6 days, on a schedule the garrison believes is secret
dataBlock.Break contact: by T+0:14 — the QRF lance reaches the ambush grid at T+0:22
dataBlock.Dispersal deadline: below 4-person thermal signature by T+0:40, when the VTOL sweep begins

sidebarKernel.kernel: Two 'Mechs against one escort 'Mech is the only fair fight this campaign will ever offer — the discipline that ends it at T+0:14 with trucks still burning, instead of letting it become a pursuit.

phases.name: AFTERMATH
phases.lead: The strike runs 11 minutes; the reprisal arithmetic runs 30 days. The third phase is staying invisible while the garrison makes the district pay, and not flinching in front of the people who carry the bill.

dataBlock.Reprisal schedule: nearest work brigade to half ration credits for 30 days; 3 levee captains detained for interrogation
dataBlock.Informer market: bounty doubles after the second convoy loss and pays in protein ration, not scrip
dataBlock.Courier discipline: all routes cold for 6 days after any strike; reopened only by the chalk signal
dataBlock.Cover verdict: one verification cycle completed with zero flags = the census still believes the cell does not exist

sidebarKernel.kernel: The two-column ledger read aloud after each strike: what the cell spent in rounds and fuel against what the district paid in ration credits and detentions.

title: OPERATION BAD DEBT
skeleton: a stranded stay-behind company must sustain a documented-effect harassment campaign against an occupier's logistics on a filter-rationed clock, while a counterintelligence service ignores the battlefield and starves the company by turning the worker towns whose coal each strike costs
inspiration: interdiction campaign against an occupied mining district decided by a dust-fouled logistics-attrition ledger — the Donbas pit-country raiding of 1943
situation: {WORLD}, {YEAR}. The world fell to {TARGET_FACTION} 7 months ago and your company did not leave with the rest of the garrison, because Annex F of the contract with {EMPLOYER} includes a stay-behind clause and your commanding officer signed it. The terms: 200 days of harassment operations against the occupation's logistics, with pay held in an offworld escrow account and the completion bonus paid only if you can document the damage you do. Salvage rights are technically yours but practically worthless — there is no way to lift captured tonnage off a blockaded world. The operating area is the Ash Belt: a 40-kilometer arc of open-pit lignite (brown coal) terraces between the foundry plant and the spaceport. The terrace faces drop 12 meters at each cut, haul roads zigzag between them, and the only fast routes are the ones the enemy watches. Coal dust is both your biggest terrain problem and your cover: it scatters thermal signatures, fouls magscan near the ore bodies, and holds visibility to 300-600 meters even on a still day. It also damages machines — every field operation burns through air and coolant filter sets, and the company has only 26 of them. The only resupply is through {NPC:fixer} at the rail junction, a freight agent who sells both information and parts, in both directions, at a 400 percent markup and payment up front. Around the pits live 19,000 miners in 5 company towns. The occupation pays them for coal quotas in scrip and winter heating allotments, and punishes sabotage by docking the nearest town's quota 15 percent per incident. Winter arrives in roughly 40 days, though that figure comes from pre-war mining almanacs, not this year's weather. So the moral cost is simple and ugly. Every raid you run is paid for twice: once by the enemy in lost supplies, and once by the towns in coal they will not have to burn in January. A {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence team under {NPC:counterintel-hunter} arrived 3 weeks ago. The report is 6 days old and rated reliable, bought at the rail junction at the usual markup. They are not searching the terraces. They are working the towns, because they have done the same math you have and they know it is the townspeople who will talk. Enemy garrison: 1 'Mech company (Regular, medium-heavy), 1 armor company, and 1 infantry battalion at the spaceport 22 kilometers from the Belt's eastern edge, plus an aerospace pair at the polar airstrip. Your company is the only friendly force on {WORLD}, and the escrow account will pay out on results regardless of what those results cost.

objectives.primary: Keep up the harassment for 200 days: at least 1 confirmed strike against the plant-to-spaceport supply line every 10 days.
objectives.secondary: Keep the company's combat strength above 60 percent. If it drops below that, the escrow contract's penalty clause activates and cuts your pay.
objectives.bonus: Deliver an intelligence file on the foundry plant's export schedule to the {EMPLOYER} pickup at day 200.

complications.name: Proof of Effect
complications.text: The escrow agent requires gun-camera footage plus independent corroboration for each credited interdiction. Hitting a target and leaving is not enough; the contract wants evidence shot from inside the engagement envelope.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The unit must remain at each objective 2 additional turns after mission completion to document effect, or the interdiction does not count toward the 10-day tempo requirement.

complications.name: Filter Math
complications.text: Coal dust destroys air and coolant filters fast. The company starts with 26 filter sets, and each field operation in the Belt burns 1 to 3 of them depending on how long it lasts and how hard the wind blows. The only resupply is the rail-junction fence, and the more desperate the company gets, the more he charges.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track filter sets as a campaign resource. At 8 or fewer, 'Mechs operate at +1 heat in the Belt; at 0, field operations stop until purchase. Fence resupply: 400 percent of book price, 6-day lead time, 25 percent chance per purchase that the transaction is reported to the counterintel team.

complications.name: First Snow
complications.text: When winter closes in, ambient cold raises the thermal contrast of a running fusion plant against the terraces. The dust that hid you settles under snow crust.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After first snowfall (roll from day 35 onward), enemy thermal detection range increases 50 percent at night and the Belt's concealment bonus drops one step.

complications.name: Quota Dock
complications.text: Each interdiction docks the nearest pit town's coal quota 15 percent for the quarter. The towns keep their own ledger of what your campaign has cost them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a quota-dock total per town. Any town at a cumulative 45 percent dock produces an informer: the company's nearest cache or hide in that town's sector is compromised within 5 days.

decisionPoints.name: What the Belt Eats
decisionPoints.context: Three different systems carry the plant's output to the spaceport, and the company can wreck any one of them faster than the enemy can repair it. Each choice sends the cost to a different place: slow contract credit, the worst enemy security in the Belt, or 19,000 civilians losing their heat.

options.title: The Haul Road Bridges
advantages: Low repair priority for the enemy — output slows 30 percent rather than stopping, which keeps the reprisal response proportionate
Demolition work, minimal exposure: 2-'Mech missions, in and out inside 40 minutes
disadvantages: Slow contract math: bridge kills credit at half value under the proof-of-effect annex
The enemy reroutes within 8 days per bridge and the Belt only has 6 bridges
options.consequence: Sustainable tempo through day 120, after which the bridge inventory is exhausted and the remaining targets are the two you were avoiding.

costs.resource: filter sets: 1-2 per 2-'Mech mission, from a stock of 26
costs.risk: half-value contract credit per bridge kill — the 6-bridge inventory runs out by day 120

options.title: The Rail Spur
advantages: Highest credited value per strike — the spur carries 70 percent of export tonnage
One good cut stops shipments for 12-15 days
disadvantages: {TARGET_FACTION} counterintelligence saturates the spur corridor after the first cut: sensor posts every 2 kilometers, inspection patrols at 90-minute intervals
Reaction timeline at the spur is the worst in the Belt — open approaches both sides
options.consequence: Two spur cuts likely satisfy a full quarter of the tempo requirement, and after the first one the spur becomes the most dangerous place on {WORLD}.

costs.resource: filter sets: 2-3 per strike; after the first cut, the spur corridor — sensor posts every 2 kilometers, patrols at 90-minute intervals
costs.risk: open approaches both sides; the worst reaction timeline in the Belt

options.title: The Power Trunk
advantages: Cutting the plant's transmission trunk stops exports for an estimated 20 days
The trunk towers stand in dead ground the garrison cannot overwatch without dedicating its aerospace pair
disadvantages: The same trunk powers the pit towns' heating grid — cutting it in winter leaves 19,000 people with no heat
The enemy will force town residents to do the repair work at gunpoint: your sabotage becomes their forced labor
options.consequence: Maximum contract credit and maximum quota-dock acceleration; the towns' informer thresholds drop 15 percent the day the lights go out.

costs.resource: the pit towns' heating grid — 19,000 people's winter heat rides the same trunk
costs.risk: informer thresholds drop 15 percent the day the lights go out; quota-dock totals accelerate toward the 45 percent compromise line

decisionPoints.name: Thirty Names
decisionPoints.context: The counterintel team takes 30 hostages from Pit Town Three and broadcasts terms: the mercenary commander surrenders within 100 hours or the thirty stand trial for banditry under occupation law. The broadcast repeats every 2 hours on the public band.

options.title: Go Dark
advantages: The company survives intact and the campaign tempo can resume after the deadline passes
No operational information is exposed by any contact or response
disadvantages: The trials proceed; sentences under occupation banditry law run 10 years to capital
Pit Town Three and its neighbors close to the company permanently — caches, eyes, silence, all gone
options.consequence: The campaign continues, but the local population now has 30 fresh reasons to inform on the company to the occupier, and the quota-dock informer thresholds drop by 15 percent across all towns.

costs.resource: Pit Town Three and its neighbors — caches, eyes, silence — closed to the company permanently
costs.risk: 30 sentences of 10 years to capital; informer thresholds drop 15 percent across all towns

options.title: Trade a Cache
advantages: The counterintel service has historically honored materiel-for-release exchanges to build informant trust
30 releases buys back the towns' tolerance for another quarter
disadvantages: The surrendered cache hands {NPC:counterintel-hunter} forensic leads: lot numbers, packing patterns, supplier traces
Proves to the counterintel service that hostage-taking works on this unit; expect it again at day 140
options.consequence: Hostages released. The counterintel service works the cache evidence toward the rail junction fence within 20 days, and your resupply line becomes a surveillance operation pointed back at you.

costs.resource: one full supply cache, surrendered with its lot numbers, packing patterns, and supplier traces
costs.risk: the counterintel service reaches the rail-junction fence within 20 days; hostage-taking is proven to work — expect a repeat near day 140

options.title: Hit the Detention Siding
advantages: The hostages are held in 2 railcars at a known siding pending transport — a target the company can actually reach
Success converts the towns from neutral terrain to active support overnight
disadvantages: Open battle inside town limits, civilians inside the engagement envelope, the counterintel guard force fights from among the railcars
Casualties among the people being rescued are probable, not just possible
options.consequence: Win or lose, the occupation re-classifies the operating area from banditry suppression to active counterinsurgency: garrison reinforcement request goes offworld within a week, and the back half of the contract is played against a doubled OpFor.

costs.resource: open battle inside town limits with civilians and the rescued inside the engagement envelope
costs.risk: reclassification to active counterinsurgency — the contract's back half plays against a doubled OpFor

entries.event: Rail spur strike initiated; line sensors trip and the garrison TOC logs the alarm.
Ready lance at the spaceport ordered to mount; aerospace pair at the polar strip warned.
Ready lance departs spaceport, 22 kilometers, vectoring for the haul-road junctions to cut the Belt exits.
VTOL reconnaissance up, sweeping bench lines along the probable egress fan.
Ready lance reaches the spur. Interception geometry on the haul roads now favors the enemy.
Aerospace pair on station over the Belt with full daylight loiter.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Break contact and get under a terrace overhang or into the dust cloud by T+0:34. After T+0:55 the aerospace pair controls every open terrace until nightfall, and a 'Mech caught on an open switchback road in daylight will be destroyed — a loss that also pushes the company toward the escrow penalty clause.

opforSketch.composition: {TARGET_FACTION} garrison battalion: 1 'Mech company (Regular, medium-heavy mix with 1 Veteran command lance), 1 armor company (tracked, road-bound in the Belt), 1 infantry battalion, aerospace pair (Regular). Counterintelligence detachment, 12-20 agents (Veteran), operating in the towns. Generator weights pursuit speed and sensor assets over tonnage.
opforSketch.behavior: Garrison doctrine is face-conscious and methodical: hard pursuit once contact is made, reluctance to report failure upward, which produces overcommitment on bad terrain. The counterintel service runs the real campaign — patient, town-focused, treating the company as a logistics problem to be starved rather than a force to be fought.

forks.name: OPERATION PAID IN FULL
forks.trigger: Tempo requirement met through day 200 with company strength above 60 percent.
forks.consequence: Extraction lift arrives at the day-200 window; escrow plus bonus releases. {EMPLOYER} offers a follow-on raiding contract against the {WORLD} approaches at improved rates — the company now being the acknowledged expert on the target.

forks.name: OPERATION ESCROW
forks.trigger: Tempo missed for 2 consecutive cycles, or company strength below 60 percent.
forks.consequence: {EMPLOYER} invokes the penalty clause: no lift. The company self-extracts via {NPC:smuggler-captain}, whose price is every BattleMech the company cannot fit in one DropShip bay plus 18 months of discretion it cannot verify.

forks.name: OPERATION COLD PIT
forks.trigger: The counterintel service localizes the company's quarry hide via informer or cache forensics.
forks.consequence: Combined garrison assault on the hide with aerospace overwatch. The company fights a survival action and disperses to alternate hides with whatever it can carry, then rebuilds tempo from caches — the contract clock does not pause for being hunted.

storyElementSeed: Two techs argue in whispers over which machine gets the last clean filter set, then stop arguing and split the set between intake banks; the heater in the maintenance bay stays cold either way, and the argument resumes tomorrow over a different part.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Hold the line item: 1 verified interdiction per 10-day cycle, 200 days. Nobody is coming early. Document everything — the relief force's planners will build the counter-landing around what you prove the enemy cannot protect.

resourceGates.lackingText: No friendly depot on {WORLD}: every option's filter spend reprices at the rail-junction fence's terms — 400 percent of book, payment in advance, 6-day lead, 25 percent chance per purchase the transaction is reported to the counterintel team.

phases.name: LAYING-IN
phases.lead: Before dropping the first bridge, the company has to build its support network: hide sites, supply caches, and a careful count of its filter sets. In the Ash Belt, anything improvised after the shooting starts tends to get the company killed — it all has to be in place beforehand.

dataBlock.Filter stock: 26 sets at day 1; 1-3 consumed per field operation depending on duration and wind
dataBlock.Cache plan: 6 caches across the Belt, no single cache holding more than 15 percent of any commodity
dataBlock.Resupply: rail-junction fence only — 400 percent of book, payment in advance, 6-day lead, 25 percent report risk per purchase
dataBlock.Proof-of-effect rig: gun-camera plus independent corroboration; 2 additional turns on every objective

phases.protocol: All fence contact runs through 1 buyer and 1 alternate, never armed, never in company gear. Orders are placed by matching torn-banknote serials; pickup is 6 days later at the third coal tipple — payment left, goods taken, no meeting, no conversation. The fence never sees a face he could sell twice.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The 26-set filter ledger as the campaign's true calendar: which targets are worth a set, and the day the answer changes.

phases.name: TEMPO
phases.lead: One verified interdiction per 10-day cycle, 20 cycles. The Belt offers bridges, the rail spur, and the power trunk; the contract counts effect, the towns count cost, and both ledgers are accurate.

routes.name: Route SOOT
routes.desc: the worked-out third-level bench, 9 kilometers under cut overhang, dust pall permanent

title: OPERATION STANDPIPE
skeleton: a merchant-funded ward resistance must retake the captive water plant its whole population drinks from intact, against a pirate landlord who will fly the plant's irreplaceable heart offworld the moment he judges the asset lost
inspiration: seizing a critical waterworks held hostage by an occupying band — the contest for the Tikrit barrage pumping stations, 2003
situation: {WORLD}, {YEAR}. {DISTRICT} has no real government — just a web of informal deals between local powers. Five weeks ago a pirate crew calling itself the Brine Court broke the one deal that mattered: they seized the Vitric Works, the cracking and desalination plant that supplies drinking water to the eastern wards of {WORLD}, where 31,000 people collect a daily ration at 9 public standpipes. The Brine Court's commander {NPC:opfor-commander} now sells that water back to the wards at triple the old price and shoots people who jump the queue, as a way of enforcing it. {EMPLOYER} — a group of eastern-ward merchants who understand numbers — is funding the resistance because a thirsty population is bad for business. The resistance is you: 19 fighters, 26 working rifles, 4 SRM reloads, and 2 BattleMechs, one of them with a seized left elbow actuator nobody has the parts to fix. That is your entire force, and every operation uses it up. The terrain works against you. The Vitric Flats are a 6-kilometer ring of fused glass-slag desert between the wards and the Works — the floor of an old industrial fire. The glass crust cracks under a 'Mech's weight (footing checks every 500 meters) and shreds wheeled vehicles' tires within 2 kilometers, though hovercraft cross it cleanly. When the wind picks up, glass-dust storms (locals call them a glass-out) drop visibility to 150 meters, chew up air filters, and ground the Brine Court's spotter ultralights. The wards themselves are shanty terraces with streets only 3 to 5 meters wide: no 'Mech can enter and none ever has, so fighting there comes down to rifles and knowing the staircases. Your fighters hide in the water queues, because a crowd at a standpipe is the one place no one looks twice. But that cover has a price: when fighters shot a Brine Court patrol 200 meters from Standpipe 4, the Court cut that ward's ration to 1.5 liters per person per day for a week, and the ward blamed the fighters, not the Court. Every time you use the queues for cover, the people in them pay for it. Brine Court strength: 40 to 60 fighters (Green and Regular, with a Veteran core guard of 8), 6 to 9 armed technicals, 2 BattleMechs in working order, and 1 old cargo lighter parked on the pan hardstand. If the Court ever decides it is losing, that lighter can carry the plant's membrane stacks offworld. This picture is 4 days old and rated fair, from {NPC:resistance-leader} inside the plant's forced-labor shift. The membrane stacks are everything: they are the one part that makes the plant work, and there is no replacement within many jumps. If the plant is wrecked, all 31,000 people lose their water. So there are only two ways to win: take the plant with the stacks still in it, or stop the lighter from carrying them off.

objectives.primary: Seize the Vitric Works pumphouse and control room intact, with membrane stacks in place and functioning.
objectives.secondary: Keep eastern-ward queue ration above 2 liters per person per day for the campaign's duration.
objectives.bonus: Capture the Brine Court's cargo lighter on the pan hardstand before it can lift.

complications.name: Glass-Out
complications.text: Wind over 40 kph lifts the Flats into a glass-dust storm: visibility 150 meters, comms degraded, filters consumed at triple rate. The Court's ultralights ground and their gun crews button up. It is the best assault weather the world offers and it costs equipment to use.
complications.mechanicalEffect: During glass-out: visibility caps at 150 meters, all indirect fire spotting fails, ambushes gain surprise one step easier, and every machine operating outside consumes 3x filter stock.

complications.name: Queue Reprisal
complications.text: Any fighting within 500 meters of an active standpipe gets that ward's water ration cut as punishment — the Court answers every security incident by taking water from the civilians nearby.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each such engagement: affected ward's ration drops to 1.5 L/day for 7 days and the ward's unrest counter rises 1. At unrest 3, the ward sells a cell hide-site location to the Court within 48 hours.

complications.name: The Lighter Clock
complications.text: The Court's lighter can be loaded with the plant's membrane stacks in roughly 40 minutes by pressed labor. The moment the Court's commander judges the plant lost, the membranes start coming out of the racks.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Once any assault reaches the Works perimeter, start a 40-minute extraction clock (see reaction timeline). If the lighter lifts loaded, the primary objective becomes permanently unachievable.

decisionPoints.name: The Smuggler's Price
decisionPoints.context: {NPC:smuggler-captain} grounds at the pan's free anchorage with 4 tons of munitions and 200 filter sets for sale — and a documented history of selling cargo manifests to whoever asks nicely with money. The cell needs the cargo. The question is the currency.

options.title: Pay in Water Scrip
advantages: Preserves the cell's combat assets — both 'Mechs stay in the order of battle
Scrip is the one currency the cell can replenish through {EMPLOYER}
disadvantages: Scrip spends at the Works gate too: the smuggler will trade it onward to the Brine Court for fuel
A large scrip movement tells anyone watching the anchorage how the wards are funding their war
options.consequence: Cargo secured; within 10 days the Court knows the resistance's funding scale, and {NPC:opfor-commander} raises the water price to drain the scrip pool faster than the merchants can refill it.

costs.resource: water scrip: the full cargo price, replenishable only through {EMPLOYER}'s merchants
costs.risk: the scrip movement prices the resistance's funding scale for anyone watching the anchorage — the Court raises water prices within 10 days

options.title: Pay with the Lame 'Mech
advantages: The seized-elbow machine converts from maintenance burden to purchasing power
The smuggler values hulls over paper and will deal exclusively for hardware
disadvantages: The order of battle drops to one BattleMech, permanently, against a foe with two
Watching a 'Mech walk onto a stranger's lighter does measurable damage to fighter morale
options.consequence: Best price and a discreet seller, but every plan for the Works assault must now work with a single 'Mech — and the Court's two will learn they outnumber you the first time it matters.

costs.resource: 1 BattleMech (seized left elbow actuator) — the order of battle drops to one machine, permanently
costs.risk: measurable fighter morale damage; the Court's two 'Mechs learn the arithmetic the first time it matters

options.title: Pay in Intelligence
advantages: Costs no scrip, no hardware: the cell trades its map of the Brine Court's offworld buyer circuit
Establishes the cell as an information peer the smuggler will want to keep trading with
disadvantages: Burns the cell's only strategic leverage over the Court's revenue
Coin flip whether the smuggler resells the cell's order book to the Court inside a week — his record supports it
options.consequence: Cargo secured and a relationship opened; 50 percent chance the Court learns the cell's strength and supply state within 7 days and times its next sweep accordingly.

costs.resource: the cell's map of the Brine Court's offworld buyer circuit — its only strategic leverage over Court revenue, spent
costs.risk: 50 percent the order book is resold to the Court inside 7 days

decisionPoints.name: Intact or Ours
decisionPoints.context: The assault on the Works has one real objective: take the pumphouse and control room with the membrane stacks still in their racks. There are three ways in, and each one risks something the wards cannot replace — the pumps themselves, the membranes' survival, or the assault's surprise.

options.title: Storm the Pumphouse First
advantages: Fastest route to the only objective that counts; the extraction clock never starts if the control room falls in the first 10 minutes
The night shift is 14 pressed workers who will go to the floor, not fight
disadvantages: Fighting inside the pumphouse risks the pumps themselves — a stray SRM into the manifold gallery is a city-killer
The approach crosses 400 meters of open pan under the gate gun
options.consequence: Success ends the campaign in one night. Any weapon discharge heavier than rifle caliber inside the pumphouse rolls against the manifold, and a manifold hit puts the wards on 1 liter per day for a month no matter who wins.

costs.resource: 400 meters of open pan crossed under the gate gun
costs.risk: any discharge above rifle caliber rolls against the manifold — a hit puts 31,000 people on 1 liter per day for a month, win or lose

options.title: Cut Power, Assault Dark
advantages: Dropping the plant's feeder kills the perimeter lights, the gate gun's traverse motor, and the Court's comms repeater in one action
The cell's fighters know the dark plant from pressed-labor shifts; the Court's gunmen do not
disadvantages: Unpowered pumps let the membrane stacks begin crystallizing after 6 hours — the assault must win and restore power inside that window
The Court's 'Mechs run on their own reactors and lose nothing
options.consequence: The fight happens on the cell's terms in the dark, against a hard 6-hour engineering deadline that does not care how the fight is going.

costs.resource: the membrane stacks' 6-hour crystallization clock, started by the cell's own hand
costs.risk: the assault must win and restore power inside 6 hours; the Court's 'Mechs run on their own reactors and lose nothing

options.title: Buy the Gate Shift
advantages: The Court's gate crew are hired locals paid in the same scrip as everyone — 3 of 5 are from the eastern wards
A walked-in assault skips the pan crossing and the gate gun entirely
disadvantages: 40 percent chance per approach the bribed man takes the money and reports the offer anyway — the Court pays informer bounties in water rights
Sets a price on betrayal that the Court can outbid next week, against you
options.consequence: If the bribe holds, the Works falls with under a dozen shots fired. If it breaks, the assault walks into a prepared kill zone at the gate and the extraction clock starts before the first round lands.

costs.resource: bribe in water scrip to 3 of 5 gate crew, plus a posted price on betrayal the Court can outbid next week
costs.risk: 40 percent per approach the bribed man takes the money and reports — the assault then walks into a prepared kill zone

6 technicals roll from the pan gate to skirmish line on the inner Flats.
Court 'Mechs begin cold-start sequence — 9 minutes from horn to movement.
Both Court 'Mechs on the Flats, working the cairn lanes between glass-shear zones they have mapped and you have not.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Secure the control room by T+0:25, or the membranes start coming out of the racks. At T+0:40 the lighter lifts off with them, leaving the Vitric Works as 40,000 tons of empty pipework that can no longer make water. After that, the eastern wards' water has to be hauled in as ice from the southern mine — a 9-day round trip — and the whole campaign will have been for nothing.

opforSketch.composition: Pirate band, 40-60 fighters (Green/Regular, 8-strong Veteran core guard), 6-9 armed technicals, 2 BattleMechs (mismatched salvage, one Regular pilot, one Green), fixed gate gun, 1 cargo lighter. Generator should produce a ragged light/medium pair with ammunition-poor loadouts and one nasty surprise weapon.
opforSketch.behavior: The Brine Court holds the Works as revenue, not ground: it fights to preserve assets, threatens the membranes as a hostage when pressed, and runs rather than dies. Expect technical screens, 'Mechs held back as the bank guard, and negotiation offers timed to stall any assault past its momentum.

forks.consequence: The wards return to full water rations and {EMPLOYER} turns the cell into a paid standing militia. forks.consequence: Eastern-ward water converts to ice-haul convoys from the southern mine on a 9-day cycle, and the mission becomes convoy escort across the Flats while the wards empty — triage by neighborhood, with {EMPLOYER} deciding which standpipes go dark first.

forks.consequence: The assault meets a prepared defense and must abort into the Flats during a glass-out — footing checks, blind movement, filters burning triple — and afterward the cell must find the leak with 19 suspects and no margin for being wrong.

merc.objectives.primary: Contract object is the plant functioning, not the plant flying a new flag: pumphouse and control room intact, membranes in the racks, certified by the employer's engineer. Wreckage pays zero.

phases.name: THE WORKS
phases.lead: Everything ends at the pumphouse: a 40-minute clock on the lighter, a manifold that no weapon heavier than a rifle can be fired near, and 14 forced laborers on the night shift who will drop to the floor when the shooting starts. Take the control room before T+0:25 or the membranes — the only thing that makes the plant work — fly away offworld.

dataBlock.Extraction clock: T+0:25 membranes start leaving the racks; T+0:40 lighter loaded and lift-capable
dataBlock.Gate gun: fixed mount commanding the 400-meter open pan approach
dataBlock.Night shift: 14 pressed workers, non-combatant, known to the cell by name
dataBlock.Manifold rule: nothing above rifle caliber discharges inside the pumphouse — a manifold hit puts the wards on 1 liter per day for a month, win or lose

A red flare means manifold threatened — all weapons tight. The word KETTLE on the working channel means lighter loading observed: every gun that can bear shifts to the pan hardstand.

Left elbow actuator seized; the arm weapon trains only by full torso rotation. No parts exist on-world, and the smuggler values the hull at full price anyway — which is its own kind of temptation.

Reports from inside the pressed shift at 4-day latency and can be pulled out exactly once — extraction burns the inside picture for good. Has refused 2 extraction offers already and not explained why.
Aged, single-pad, 40 minutes to load the membrane stacks with pressed labor. Whether it can lift fully fueled is UNCONFIRMED — basis: pan fuel-bowser counts via the labor shift, 4 days old.

title: OPERATION RUNNING TAB
skeleton: a fixed-stipend pirate hunt fought against its own fuel ledger across a multi-jump frontier, where the only intelligence broker sells the hunters' approach to the hunted and the lair's lava-shield landward face funnels the assault into knife range
inspiration: long-range pirate suppression bounded by coal and steaming range — the anti-slaver patrols of the West Africa Squadron, 1840s
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The Jacklighters have raided 3 frontier systems in 14 months — hijacking grain lifts, taking captives for indentured labor, and burning one JumpShip recharge station — and {EMPLOYER}, a coalition of planetary combines that insures its own shipping because no one else will, has hired you to hunt them down. The contract is a fixed fee plus a fuel allowance covering 5 jump-charges, and that allowance is the heart of the problem: your JumpShip needs 8 days to recharge on its sail, every repositioning jump uses up one charge plus the transit time, and every dead-end lead costs 12 to 16 days against a fee that never grows. The economics of the hunt are the real battlefield here. The intelligence market has one source worth using: {NPC:fixer}, a freight-paperwork fence on the {WORLD} docks who buys port manifests from ships' pursers and sells them to anyone — the combines, the hunters, and on at least one documented occasion the Jacklighters themselves. A manifest cycle costs 5,000 C-bills. Exclusivity costs 12,000, and he will not actually honor it. His information is reliable; his loyalty lasts exactly as long as you are the highest bidder. His current best information is cross-checked against the debrief of a ransomed purser. It is 26 days old and rated fair, so expect some of it to have changed. The band is based at Slag Harbor, a settled volcanic crater two jumps into the deep periphery, at an abandoned mining wharf on the crater's north shore. The purser's count of band strength: 8 to 11 BattleMechs in a beat-up mix of weights including 2 salvaged heavies, 1 Leopard DropShip, 1 Union DropShip (the Union's ability to fly is UNCONFIRMED — the purser saw it grounded with a deck plate open), 4 fixed gun pits on the headland, and 32 indentured laborers working the wharf — your employer's own citizens, taken from their home colony 8 months ago. The terrain works against you. The Graywater is a 7-kilometer stretch of active lava field between the only usable landing ground and the wharf. The flows are crusted over with uneven load-bearing strength, and the only surveyed crossing lanes are marked by stone cairns the band maintains. Off those lanes, the crust can collapse and drop a 'Mech into rock glowing at 200 degrees Celsius — and recovering it would cost more than the entire contract fee. The sensor conditions are even worse than the footing: patches of ground at 80 to 200 degrees completely blind thermal imaging — yours and theirs alike — and the iron-rich slag cuts magscan range to 400 meters. Everything that happens on the Graywater happens at very short range. Plan the approach as if the fuel gauge is the most important number on the board, because it is.

objectives.primary: Destroy or capture the Jacklighters' DropShip lift capacity and at least 50 percent of their BattleMech strength at Slag Harbor.
objectives.bonus: Recover the band's buyer manifests — the paper chain linking their prizes to a salvage network reaching deeper into the periphery, deliverable to {NPC:salvage-broker} verification.

complications.name: The Tab
complications.text: The fuel stipend covers 5 jump-charges, full stop. Dry leads, repositioning, and any withdrawal-and-return all draw from the same account, and when it empties the unit jumps home on its own C-bills or doesn't.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track jump-charges as a campaign resource starting at 5. Each system entry or repositioning costs 1. At 0, every further jump costs the unit 28,000 C-bills of its own funds, and the employer's termination option opens.

complications.name: The Fence's Other Customer
complications.text: Any intelligence purchased on the {WORLD} docks can be resold, and the Jacklighters pay standing rates for word of anyone asking about them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each intelligence purchase carries a 40 percent chance the band learns of the hunt within 10 days. If triggered before the assault, the Slag Harbor defense is prepared: gun pits pre-registered on the cairn lanes, ready 'Mechs doubled.

complications.name: Crust Collapse
complications.text: The Graywater only holds a 'Mech's weight along the cairn-marked lanes the band surveys and maintains. Step off those lanes and the crust may or may not hold — and if it gives way, the molten rock underneath is hot enough to cripple the machine.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Off-cairn movement: bearing check per 300 meters; failure drops the 'Mech through crust for falling damage plus 5 heat per turn until extracted. Extraction requires a second 'Mech and 3 turns. Cairn lanes are single-file.

complications.name: Pressed Crews
complications.text: The headland gun pits are crewed by indentured laborers under guard — the same people the contract pays you to bring home. They serve the guns badly and on purpose, but the guns still fire.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Gun pits fire at -1 effectiveness. Each pit destroyed by fire kills 1d3 indentured crew, counted against the secondary objective and against unit reputation with all frontier employers.

decisionPoints.name: Buying the Map
decisionPoints.context: The fence's manifest data would confirm the Slag Harbor lair, the band's supply schedule, and the Union's flight status — and the act of buying it is itself a commodity he can sell onward. The 26-day-old purser intelligence is the only alternative on the shelf.

options.title: Pay the 5,000
advantages: Current data: lair confirmed, supply cycle dated, Union status resolved before the unit commits a jump-charge
Keeps the only intelligence counter on the approaches open for the next contract
disadvantages: 40 percent chance the purchase is resold to the band within 10 days
Every C-bill of intelligence spend is outside the stipend — the fee eats it
options.consequence: The unit jumps on good data with a 4-in-10 chance the destination is rehearsing its arrival; the fence files the transaction either way, for futures.

costs.risk: 40 percent the purchase is resold to the band within 10 days — gun pits pre-registered, ready 'Mechs doubled

options.title: Seize His Books
advantages: Immediate, complete, free: manifests, buyer lists, and the band's own purchase history in one strongbox
Removes the leak — what he no longer has, he cannot resell
disadvantages: The port authority fines docks violence at 8,000 C-bills and suspends the unit's loading priority
Burns the only intelligence tap on the approaches permanently — no-recourse, no-return
options.consequence: Perfect data for this hunt, but no intelligence source for any hunt after it. The frontier's grey-market dealers mark the unit as one that robs its sources, and they are a tight-knit, long-memoried network that talks to each other.

costs.resource: {WORLD} loading priority, suspended; the only intelligence tap on the approaches, burned permanently
costs.risk: the frontier grey market marks the unit's name — long memories, wide family trees

options.title: Shadow the Courier
advantages: The fence's courier boat physically carries his trade to a handoff point — following it yields the band's contact procedure as well as the lair
Costs nothing and sells nothing; the fence never knows
disadvantages: 11 days of surveillance the contract clock and recharge cycle keep paying for
30 percent chance the band displaces from Slag Harbor in the interval — the purser data is already 26 days old
options.consequence: If the band sits still, the unit arrives with the best intelligence picture of all three options and total surprise; if it has moved, two jump-charges are gone and the tab is half spent on an empty caldera.

costs.resource: 11 days of contract clock and recharge cycle, spent watching a courier boat
costs.risk: 30 percent the band displaces mid-shadow — 2 jump-charges of the 5-charge tab spent on an empty caldera

decisionPoints.name: The Graywater Problem
decisionPoints.context: The lair's landward face is 7 kilometers of lava shield crossable only on the band's cairn lanes; the seaward face is the caldera harbor under 4 gun pits. Force structure must commit before anyone learns which approach the band actually fears.

options.title: Night March on the Cairn Lanes
advantages: Full force arrives together; thermal blindness on the shield works for the attacker at night
No third parties involved, no extra cost against the tab
disadvantages: Single-file movement on 2 lanes — the column has no width and no flank
If the fence sold the hunt, the lanes are pre-registered artillery solutions
options.consequence: The assault arrives as a knife-range brawl in the dark at the wharf perimeter; everything depends on whether the band knew to be awake.

costs.risk: single-file on 2 cairn lanes with no width and no flank — pre-registered artillery solutions if the fence sold the hunt

options.title: Survey a New Lane
advantages: Engineering teams with thermal probes can prove a third lane the band does not watch — 36 hours of work
Attacks the one assumption the defense is built on
disadvantages: 36 hours of survey teams exposed on the shield, with a 1-in-3 chance of a band patrol contact mid-survey
Costs the schedule; the recharge cycle and the employer's patience both keep running
options.consequence: Success delivers the only unwatched approach on the planet; a patrol contact mid-survey converts the hunt into a meeting engagement on the worst footing in the system.

costs.resource: engineering teams exposed on the shield for 36 hours while the recharge cycle and the employer's patience keep running
costs.risk: 1-in-3 band patrol contact mid-survey — a meeting engagement on the worst footing in the system

options.title: Seaward Assault by Hired Barge
advantages: Two ore barges hired at Slag Harbor settlement can land a lance inside the caldera, behind the Graywater entirely
The gun pits face seaward fire poorly — pressed crews, fixed traverse
disadvantages: Barge masters are settlement civilians whose silence is rented, not owned — the band pays mooring fees here
Splits the force: whatever lands by sea fights alone until the landward element crosses 7 kilometers
options.consequence: A bold plan that defeats the terrain problem completely if the barge masters stay loyal — and delivers a lance straight into a prepared kill zone if they sell you out.

costs.resource: 2 ore barges hired at settlement rates, outside the stipend — silence rented, not owned, in a port where the band pays the mooring fees
costs.risk: the seaward lance fights alone until the landward element crosses 7 kilometers

entries.event: Headland lookout fires the alarm flare; wharf floodlights cut; gun pit crews driven to stations.
Gun pits manned and firing on anything visible in the approach lanes.
First 3 band 'Mechs powered — hot-bunk readiness — and moving to the wharf perimeter.
Full muster: 8-11 'Mechs in fighting positions among the wharf gantries.
Leopard lift-capable with leadership, manifests, and priority loot aboard.
Union lift-capable if flight-worthy; indentured laborers herded aboard as ablative cargo if time permits.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Pin, cripple, or crater the Leopard's launch pad by T+0:30. After that, the band's leadership and the buyer manifests escape offworld, the contract's main objective fails, and the unit will have spent all 5 jump-charges to capture nothing of value. This timeline assumes the alarm goes up only at first detection; if the fence sold the band your plan, every step above happens about one-third faster.

opforSketch.composition: Pirate BattleMech force, 8-11 machines, Green-to-Regular pilots under a Veteran leader {NPC:opfor-commander} — light/medium ratty mix carrying 2 salvaged heavies as anchors. 4 fixed gun pits (pressed crews, -1 effectiveness), 1 Leopard, 1 Union (flight status UNCONFIRMED). Generator should produce mismatched loadouts, thin armor, and one machine that is much better than it looks.
opforSketch.behavior: Pirates fight for exits, not ground. The perimeter buys time for the Leopard; leadership lifts the moment the wharf is breached; pressed gun crews surrender when the leaders break orbit. The dangerous window is the first 18 minutes, when the band still believes it can win the wharf and fights like it.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN LEDGER
forks.trigger: Lift capacity destroyed or captured, 50 percent of band 'Mechs accounted for, manifests recovered.
forks.consequence: The buyer manifests map a salvage-laundering chain running deeper into the periphery. {EMPLOYER} offers a follow-on contract to roll the network's next link at a 40 percent rate improvement — with a fresh fuel stipend and the unit's pick of the Slag Harbor salvage.

forks.name: OPERATION REPO
forks.trigger: Band escapes with lift capacity intact, or unit combat losses exceed contract viability.
forks.consequence: The stipend is spent and {EMPLOYER} invokes termination. The unit works its passage home escorting ore convoys through the same approaches it just stirred up — 2 jumps of slow freight with an angry, intact pirate band loose in the dark behind it.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND ANCHORAGE
forks.trigger: Band displaced from Slag Harbor but escapes with leadership and 1 DropShip.
forks.consequence: Survivor debriefs and wharf paperwork put the band's fallback within 2 jumps — and the tab at zero. Pursue on the unit's own funds against a wounded enemy, or write the remainder off and explain the arithmetic to 32 families on the home colony.

storyElementSeed: The quartermaster tapes the fuel ledger to the mess bulkhead where the whole company can watch the number fall; nobody comments, and everybody reads it twice a day on the way past.

periphery/pirate.objectives.primary: Break the Jacklighters' lift or take it for yourselves. A band without a DropShip is a militia with bad manners; the hulls and the indenture rolls are worth more than the bounty, and the bounty payer never needs to know the difference.

resourceGates.lackingText: The fence sells for payment in advance only. Below 5,000 C-bills the manifest counter is closed and the 26-day purser debrief is the only map on the shelf.
The 8,000 C-bill docks-violence fine cannot be paid: the port converts it to a lien against the unit and loading priority stays suspended until the books balance.
No owned JumpShip: the 11-day shadow rides contract transit at 28,000 C-bills per charge-equivalent outside the stipend, and the charter crew is one more set of eyes the fence can buy.

phases.name: PURSUIT
phases.lead: The hunt is fought on a ledger before it is fought on ground: 5 jump-charges, an 8-day sail recharge, and an intelligence market that sells to both sides. Every system entered is a fifth of the war spent.

dataBlock.Jump tab: 5 stipend charges; 1 per system entry or reposition; 28,000 C-bills of unit money per charge beyond the tab
dataBlock.Fence rates: manifest cycle 5,000 C-bills; exclusivity 12,000, unenforceable; resale risk 40 percent within 10 days
dataBlock.Best picture: ransomed purser debrief, 26 days old, confidence MED

sidebarKernel.kernel: Where the JumpShip waits while the DropShip hunts — and what the 8-day sail recharge means for the plan if the band bolts mid-approach.

phases.name: CORNERING
phases.lead: Slag Harbor is approached, not assaulted: 7 kilometers of live lava shield, 2 surveyed lanes the band maintains, and sensor conditions that blind both sides. Whatever happens on the Graywater happens at knife range.

routes.name: Route ANVIL
routes.desc: the north cairn lane, 7.1 kilometers, single file, cairns maintained by the band's own survey crews
routes.tradeoff: Bears any tonnage the band's heavies use; if the fence sold the hunt, ANVIL is a pre-registered artillery solution end to end.

routes.name: Route KETTLE
routes.desc: the south cairn lane, 6.4 kilometers, single file, crossing 2 exposed flow patches near 200 degrees
routes.tradeoff: Shorter and hotter — the patches blind thermal imaging 400 meters either side, yours and theirs alike.

routes.name: Route SALTWATER
routes.desc: 2 hired ore barges from Slag Harbor settlement, landing inside the caldera behind the Graywater
routes.tradeoff: Bypasses the shield entirely on rented silence, in a port where the band pays the mooring fees; the seaward lance fights alone until the landward element crosses.

dataBlock.Magscan: degraded to 400 meters by ferrous slag
dataBlock.Thermal: blinded across ambient patches of 80-200 degrees — both sides equally
dataBlock.Off-cairn: bearing check per 300 meters; a dropped 'Mech takes falling damage plus 5 heat per turn and needs a second machine and 3 turns to extract

sidebarKernel.kernel: Which approach survives being sold — the 40 percent resale figure applied to each route in turn, before the force structure commits.

phases.name: RECKONING
phases.lead: The wharf fight runs against two pressures at once: the Leopard can lift off at T+0:30, and the gun pits are crewed by the same captives the contract pays you to bring home. Pin the DropShip, spare the gunners, seize the manifests — in that order, because that is the order the contract pays for.

dataBlock.Leopard: lift-capable T+0:30 with leadership, manifests, and priority loot aboard
dataBlock.Union: lift-capable T+0:50 if flight-worthy — UNCONFIRMED, last seen grounded with a deck plate open
dataBlock.Gun pits: 4 on the headland, pressed crews at -1; each pit destroyed by fire kills 1d3 of the people the contract pays to recover
dataBlock.The dangerous window: the first 18 minutes, while the band still believes it can win the wharf

phases.protocol: Two words carry the assault: BLACKLINE spoken twice on the company net means the Leopard is pinned, crippled, or its pad cratered — manifest party go. GLASSHOUSE means pressed crews are abandoning the pits — check fire on the headland and mark the movers as friendly traffic. No acknowledgments; the dust and slag eat half of every transmission anyway.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Salvage priorities written before the fight, not after: hulls, the manifests, and 32 people who outrank both on the reputation ledger every frontier employer reads.

assetDetails.ref: indentured laborers (32, taken from the home colony)
assetDetails.detail: 8 months pressed; 6 listed sick in the purser's debrief (UNCONFIRMED). They crew the headland pits under guard and will abandon the guns the moment the guards look elsewhere — they need a marked direction to abandon toward, designated before the first shot.

Paper, not data — kept in the Leopard's master cabin per the purser, and the band's leader knows it is the only cargo aboard that hangs him. Expect the strongbox to travel wherever he does, and to burn if he cannot.

Grounded with a deck plate open at last sighting, 26 days ago. If it flies, lift-denial is a 2-ship problem and the T+0:50 entry is a planning figure, not a promise — the assault plan needs a branch for both answers.

title: OPERATION THIN ICE
skeleton: a holdfast must recover stolen fuel and grain from its own deserters cheaply enough that the hunt does not cost more than the loss, against turncoats who know its every procedure and a tide-frozen fjord that bears a 'Mech only on tested night ice
inspiration: running down mutineers who took the ship's stores before they can sell them on — the Bounty pursuit, 1789
situation: {WORLD}, {YEAR}. Eleven weeks ago a crew calling itself the Severance — 7 BattleMechs, all of them sworn to {EMPLOYER} until the day they deserted — ran off with 2 loaded fuel barges and the season's tribute grain from 2 settlements that had paid for protection in good faith. They are holed up at the Hourglass, a fjord station on {WORLD}'s {DISTRICT} coast: a fuel-cracking plant, a barge pier, and cliff walls. The port authority wants the barges back, the grain back, and the example made so no one else tries it. It has sent you, and the hunt has to be both cheap and fast, because the economics decide whether it is worth doing at all. Your DropShip burns reaction mass that the realm can only replace at its own cracking stations. The Hourglass is one of those stations, and the deserters hold it. So the fuel you burn chasing them cannot be topped up until you take it back. If the chase costs more fuel than the barges hold, the hunt loses money. And if the hunt loses money, the tribute settlements start to wonder what their protection payments actually buy. The terrain works against you. The Hourglass narrows to 700 meters between cliff walls, and at minus 40 degrees the surface freezes over every night: 20 to 60 centimeters of black ice that will only carry a 'Mech between 02:00 and 07:00 local time, and only where it is thick — and no one knows where it is thick until a tech walks out and tests it with a hand auger. Daylight warms it and makes it unreliable again. The only alternatives are boats, exposed to the station's pintle guns, or a 30-kilometer march around the head of the fjord through cold severe enough to make 'Mech actuators brittle. Intelligence comes from {NPC:smuggler-captain}, a supplier who sells to your port and to the deserters with equal cheer. His report is 5 days old and rated fair. He is paid in fuel by both sides, so assume he updates whoever paid him last. His current picture: 4 of the 7 deserter 'Mechs kept hot and ready, roughly 60 followers in the station — families and pressed-labor techs, 12 to 20 of whom will fight as infantry — and an offworld buyer arriving in 9 days with an escort to take the barges off the deserters' hands. If that sale goes through, the deserters double their strength and the hunt is no longer affordable. One more thing: the deserters know your doctrine, your callsigns, and your recovery procedures, because until eleven weeks ago they were part of your unit.

objectives.primary: Recover both fuel barges and the tribute stores intact before the offworld buyer arrives.
objectives.secondary: Kill or capture the deserter leadership ({NPC:opfor-commander}) and break the crew as an organized force.
objectives.bonus: Take the Hourglass cracking station generator-intact, adding a second fuel node to the realm's net.

complications.name: Cold Soak
complications.text: Minus 40 and falling. Myomer stiffens, actuator housings go brittle, and a 'Mech that falls on rock or ice breaks things that bend anywhere warmer. Heat sinks run beautifully; nothing else does.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All heat sink capacity +25 percent. Any fall: +1 to critical hit chances on actuators. Flamer and inferno effects degraded one step. Infantry outside shelter takes cold attrition per 4 hours.

complications.name: Ice Roulette
complications.text: The night ice holds in some places and not others. A lane that has been drill-tested is safe; anywhere else is a gamble, and the fjord beneath the ice is 60 meters deep if the gamble fails.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Crossing on untested ice: plunge check per 'Mech per 500 meters, weighted by tonnage (40 tons and under pass on all but worst rolls; 75+ tons fail on all but best). Engineering teams can certify a 500-meter lane in 20 minutes. Plunged 'Mechs: pilot survival roll, machine recoverable only after the thaw.

complications.name: The Buyer's Clock
complications.text: An offworld buyer, due in 9 days, with escort. If the barges change hands the hunt's object is gone; if the escort arrives mid-operation the force ratio inverts.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Campaign clock: 9 days. On day 9 (roll 7-11 for variance), OpFor gains 4 additional 'Mechs (Regular) and 1 armed DropShip, and the barges depart within 24 hours.

complications.name: Provisioner's Loyalty
complications.text: Every resupply purchased from the smuggler is also a position report sold onward at 6 hours' latency. He is not a traitor; he is a market.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each purchase from {NPC:smuggler-captain}: deserters learn the unit's position and strength 6 hours later. Refusing his trade entirely: lose access to his intelligence updates, and intel confidence on OpFor status drops to LOW.

decisionPoints.name: The Offer
decisionPoints.context: Day 4. The deserters signal on the old company frequency: they will hand over both barges and their leader for amnesty for the rest, plus winter rations for the 60 in the station. The voice on the channel is one your veterans trained.

options.title: Accept the Terms
advantages: Barges, grain, and the leadership delivered without losing a machine or a day
The 60 followers — including 9 trained techs the realm is starving for — come home as labor, not corpses
disadvantages: Amnesty prices desertion at one bad winter; next season's deserters will expect terms too
Verification of the leader's identity is hard at handover — a substitute body voids the second objective and you may not know for weeks
options.consequence: Cheap, fast, and the precedent spreads: deserters now know the realm will buy them back for a tolerable price, and {EMPLOYER} knows exactly which unit set that price.

costs.resource: the amnesty's sticker price: winter rations for 60, plus a published exchange rate on desertion
costs.risk: a substitute body at the handover voids the second objective, undetected for weeks

options.title: Refuse and Assault
advantages: The precedent dies properly: desertion ends at the bottom of a fjord, with witnesses
No verification problem — the unit confirms its own results
disadvantages: The assault kills pressed techs and family members alongside fighters — skilled labor the periphery cannot mint
The deserters fight like cornered colleagues who know your doctrine and your radio habits
options.consequence: Whatever the outcome, the 60 followers' fate is decided by gunfire, and the tribute settlements will hear both versions of the story.

costs.resource: pressed techs and family members inside the assault — including 9 trained techs the realm is starving for
costs.risk: cornered colleagues who know your doctrine, callsigns, and recovery procedures

options.title: Accept, Then Take the Muster
advantages: Everything at once: barges, grain, leadership, and the crew disarmed in one place at the handover
Zero assault risk against a foe standing in formation expecting parole
disadvantages: It is treachery, plainly, and the rim's radio circuits will carry it to every port inside a season
Your own ranks include people who will refuse the order or remember following it
options.consequence: Total tactical success at the cost of the realm's parole ever being believed again — the next cornered crew, anywhere, fights to the last round, and that bill arrives forever.

costs.resource: the realm's parole, spent permanently
costs.risk: every future cornered crew on the rim fights to the last round — a bill that arrives forever

decisionPoints.name: The Crossing
decisionPoints.context: Assault geometry at the Hourglass: the station sits on the inner bowl with the pier under its guns. Three ways across, each priced in a different currency the unit is short of.

options.title: Night Ice Crossing
advantages: 02:00-07:00 window puts 'Mechs on the station side before dawn watch change
Drill-tested lanes give the heaviest machines a certified path
disadvantages: Lane certification costs 20 minutes per 500 meters with the clock running
A plunge under fire is unrecoverable until spring; the fjord keeps what it takes
options.consequence: Full combat power delivered by dawn if the lanes hold; any machine lost going through the ice is a season-long subtraction from the realm's order of battle.

costs.resource: lane certification: 20 minutes per 500 meters, spent inside the 02:00-07:00 bearing window
costs.risk: a plunge under fire is a season-long subtraction from the realm's order of battle

options.title: Boats at First Light
advantages: Fastest option: infantry and battle-armor-weight assets at the pier in 40 minutes
Bypasses every footing problem the fjord owns
disadvantages: The pier's pintle guns and the cliff-top watch own the water in daylight
'Mechs stay on the far shore as fire support only — the assault element fights without them
options.consequence: Speed for separation: the boats win quickly with surprise or bleed badly without it, and either way the 'Mechs watch from 700 meters out.

costs.resource: the 'Mechs — left on the far shore as fire support only for the assault's duration
costs.risk: pier pintle guns and the cliff-top watch own the water in daylight

options.title: Headwall March
advantages: 30 kilometers around arrives landward, behind the station's seaward-facing defense
No ice checks, no boats, no third-party eyes
disadvantages: 36 hours in cold-soak conditions — actuator attrition before contact, infantry cold casualties near-certain
Spends 1.5 days against the buyer's 9-day clock
options.consequence: The defense's geometry is broken from a direction it never planned for, paid for in machine wear, frostbite, and the most expensive currency on the board: time.

costs.resource: 36 hours of cold-soak actuator attrition and near-certain infantry cold casualties before first contact
costs.risk: 1.5 days spent against the buyer's 9-day clock

entries.event: Deserter ice-watch spots the approach; station horn; pier floodlights doused.
Barge crews begin cold-start pump-out — scuttling fuel into the fjord rather than surrendering it. Barge 1 drains to half in 90 minutes.
4 hot-readiness deserter 'Mechs move to the ice edge; mortar crews to the cliff terraces.
Mortars registered on the certified ice lanes — they know where the lanes have to be.
Leadership skiff stands by at the inner channel; if the bowl is breached, {NPC:opfor-commander} runs for the headwall caves.
Barge 1 at half capacity; barge 2 pump-out begins.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Stop the pumps by T+1:30, or the fuel you recover drops below the hunt's break-even point. Past that point the operation costs the realm more than it brings back, the port authority's frustration turns directly into worse contract terms for your unit, and the tribute settlements spend the winter learning that their protection payments did not actually protect them.

opforSketch.composition: 7 deserter BattleMechs (Regular — trained to the realm's own doctrine, mixed light/medium with 1 heavy), 12-20 irregular infantry from the followers, 2 mortar positions, pier pintle guns. Generator should mirror the hunting unit's own doctrine and counters — these crews trained beside the players' formation.
