opforSketch.behavior: Defensive, fuel-as-hostage strategy: every escalation is answered with another hour of pump-out. Leadership keeps an escape route warm. They will reopen negotiation at every point where they are losing, and they know exactly which of your channels to call.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL BUNKER
forks.trigger: Both barges recovered above break-even, leadership taken, station generator intact.
forks.consequence: The realm gains a second fuel station and extends its protection network 2 systems outward. The unit gets first claim on Hourglass fuel for 12 months — and the offworld buyer, arriving to find the deal dead, now regards the realm as a power worth watching out for.

forks.name: OPERATION LEAN WINTER
forks.trigger: Fuel scuttled below break-even, or barges sold and lifted before recovery.
forks.consequence: The tithe fails. Two tributary settlements refuse next season's payment, citing the obvious, and the unit spends the winter on collection patrols that are half punitive expedition and half begging — with the whole rim watching how the realm handles being told no.

forks.name: OPERATION PROVISIONER'S BILL
forks.trigger: The smuggler's double game exposed mid-operation — the deserters demonstrate knowledge of the unit's timetable.
forks.consequence: The crossing meets a prepared ice ambush: mortars on the certified lanes, charges under the thick ice. Afterward the question is what to do about a provisioner the port cannot eat without and cannot trust — and every answer costs the supply line that keeps the hunt flying.

storyElementSeed: A tech walks the ice lane at 03:00 with a hand auger and a chalk pot, drilling, reading, marking, fifty meters at a stretch; the chalk numbers are the difference between a crossing and a funeral, and the tech's hands stop working right around the twentieth hole.

merc.objectives.primary: Recover both barges above the break-even line in annex B — the employer pays on recovered tonnage, not on effort, and fuel scuttled into a fjord appears on no invoice anyone honors.

resourceGates.lackingText: No depot draw: winter rations for 60 come out of the unit's own hold, and the recovered-fuel break-even line moves the wrong way before a single pump stops.

phases.name: INVESTMENT
phases.lead: The Hourglass can be neither rushed nor waited out: 9 days to the buyer, a provisioner who sells to both shores, and an enemy that reads your traffic because it used to write it. The first days seal the fjord and re-key everything the Severance already knows.

dataBlock.Buyer clock: 9 days (variance 7-11); on arrival the OpFor gains 4 'Mechs and 1 armed DropShip, and the barges depart within 24 hours
dataBlock.Provisioner latency: every purchase from {NPC:smuggler-captain} reaches the deserters as a position report 6 hours later
dataBlock.Station picture: 4 of 7 'Mechs at hot readiness, roughly 60 followers, 12-20 of whom will fight (5 days old — confidence MED)

phases.protocol: Day-1 re-key: every challenge table, recovery beacon, and medevac codeword the Severance trained on is burned. New authentication is a daily two-word challenge drawn from the paymaster's ledger pages, never broadcast twice. The old company frequency stays open and monitored — anything offered on it is negotiation or bait, never orders. Recovery vehicles stage off-doctrine, because the deserters wrote the doctrine's staging annex.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Who is authorized to answer the old frequency when the amnesty offer comes — decided on day 1, in writing, not at day 4 with a voice your veterans trained on the channel.

phases.name: THE CROSSING
phases.lead: Three ways onto the station side — night ice, boats at first light, the 30-kilometer headwall — each priced in a currency the unit is short of: certified lanes, daylight cover, time. The fjord does not negotiate and neither does the thermometer.

dataBlock.Bearing window: 02:00-07:00 local, night ice only; thickness 20-60 centimeters, and nobody knows where it is thick until a tech walks it
dataBlock.Lane certification: 20 minutes per 500-meter lane per engineering team, auger holes at 50-meter stretches
dataBlock.Plunge: pilot survival roll; the machine stays under the ice until the thaw
dataBlock.Cold soak: minus 40 and falling — falls add +1 to actuator criticals; infantry outside shelter attrits per 4 hours

sidebarKernel.kernel: The auger tech's chalk numbers as the operation's load-bearing document — and how long hands last at minus 40, with the relief schedule for hole twenty written before hole one.

phases.name: THE BOWL
phases.lead: Inside the bowl the fight is against pumps as much as people: scuttling starts at T+0:05 and the break-even line drains with Barge 1. The deserters fight like men who know your doctrine, because they do, and their leader keeps a skiff warm at the inner channel.

dataBlock.Pump-out: Barge 1 to half capacity in 90 minutes from T+0:05; Barge 2 begins at T+1:30
dataBlock.Break-even: pumps stopped by T+1:30 or the hunt runs at a loss
dataBlock.Mortars: registered on the certified ice lanes from T+0:25 — they know where the lanes have to be
dataBlock.Bolt-hole: leadership skiff at the inner channel; headwall caves beyond

phases.protocol: Parole procedure if any element strikes colors mid-fight: weapons grounded on the ice, crews walked to the pier head under 2 guards, no contact with the followers' quarters. The identity of {NPC:opfor-commander} is confirmed against the company muster book by 2 veterans who served beside him — before anything is signed, paid, or believed.

sidebarKernel.kernel: Fuel recovered versus fuel burned recovering it: the running break-even figure, updated aloud at every pump report, because the hunt's object is the arithmetic.

assetDetails.detail: Served inside your formation until eleven weeks ago and knows the unit's callsigns, channels, and recovery staging by heart — assume any radio message you conveniently intercept was planted by him to mislead you. At any handover or capture, confirming his identity is the weak point of the second objective: a substitute body satisfies it falsely, and the swap may go unnoticed for weeks.

The realm's actual prize — 9 certified techs the periphery cannot mint. They will not fight and will not run on night ice; each one killed in an assault is a year of capability gone, and the port authority counts in exactly those units.

Rigged for pump-out, not demolition — the deserters drain rather than blow. Boarding parties go for the pump manifolds, not the wheelhouses: the valves open at T+0:05 and Barge 1 reaches half capacity in 90 minutes.

title: OPERATION TWICE SOLD
skeleton: a payment-in-kind pirate hunt under an auditing liaison's pen must retake a hostage waterworks across a tide-gated coral shelf, where the lair is wired to blow and the only manifest fence sells the hunters' plan to the hunted
inspiration: amphibious reduction of a fortified reef strongpoint over a tidal flat — the Tarawa lagoon assault, 1943
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The Red Ledger have raided 2 rim systems near {WORLD} in 11 months, and the realm's district defense command has finally done the thing it hates most: hired outsiders. The contract is written as if the command expects you to rob them. Payment is in kind only — fuel, munitions, dock time, not a single C-bill — and any expenditure above 1 fuel load has to be countersigned by the realm's liaison, {NPC:employer-contact}, who travels with the command staff and audits everything with real dedication. The liaison is not an obstacle to work around; the liaison's signature is how the contract actually functions, so plan around it. Target: the Red Ledger's base on a rim world 2 jumps away — specifically the Meridian Atoll, a mothballed Star League desalination plant 90 kilometers offshore that the band has reoccupied. That plant is the asset the contract is priced on: the district wants it returned in working order, and the payment-in-kind schedule was calculated assuming a functioning plant. If it gets wrecked, the contract drops to bounty-only terms, a 60 percent cut in your pay. The terrain works against you. The Combs are an 11-kilometer coral shelf between the shoreline and the atoll, only 0.4 to 1.1 meters deep at low tide. 'Mechs cross at walking speed with footing checks, hovercraft cross freely, and tracked and wheeled vehicles cannot cross at all. Low tide comes twice a day, and the crossing windows last 60 to 100 minutes depending on the moon. Band strength, from the source named below, is 16 days old and rated low — treat every number as a floor: 9 BattleMechs, Green to Regular, including 2 PPC-armed heavies kept on the lagoon causeways; 2 DropShips, of which 1 can probably fly; 4 shore batteries crewed by fishermen captured in the band's last raid; and a fighting strength of 60 to 80. There is also a manifest entry, 11 days old, recording a sale of primacord and demolition charges to a Red Ledger buyer — UNCONFIRMED, but it suggests the plant is wired to blow. The intelligence source is the whole problem. {NPC:fixer}, on a rim trade port, is the only manifest fence on the circuit, and he sells port-traffic data to anyone with money — including the Red Ledger's own buyer, who is a regular customer at the same counter. Whatever you buy from him, assume the band can buy the fact that you bought it. Every plan has to survive being sold to the enemy.

objectives.primary: End the Red Ledger as a raiding force: destroy or capture both DropShips, or destroy 60 percent of band BattleMech strength.
objectives.secondary: Take the Meridian Atoll desalination plant intact — the contract's payment schedule is priced on its return to service.
objectives.bonus: Recover the rim-world registry bonds (stolen ship papers) the band uses to launder prizes, deliverable to {NPC:employer-contact}.

complications.name: Liaison Veto
complications.text: Any operation spending more than 1 fuel load requires the realm's liaison's countersignature, and the liaison signs nothing without reading it twice. Emergency spending without signature is recoverable only by post-action justification — or not at all.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Operations above 1 fuel load: 6-hour approval delay. Unsigned emergency spend: 30 percent chance it is ruled a contract breach, deducted from the payment-in-kind balance at double value.

complications.name: Typhoon Season
complications.text: The rim world in this season throws a storm cell across the barrier line every week or so. Aerospace grounds, the Combs close under 3 meters of surge, and everything waits.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each 72-hour window: 1-in-3 chance of typhoon. During typhoon: no aerospace either side, Combs impassable, shore batteries blind beyond 500 meters. Storms end in 12-36 hours.

complications.name: Pressed Gunners
complications.text: The shore batteries are crewed by fishermen taken at the band's last raid, serving under guard. They aim badly on purpose. The realm's public opinion counts every one of them as a citizen, and the district command reads casualty reports aloud in council.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Shore batteries fire at -1 effectiveness. Each battery destroyed by fire: 1d3 pressed crew killed, each counted against unit standing with the realm; 3+ total deaths halve the bonus objective payout and close one future contract with the realm.

complications.name: Scuttle Charges
complications.text: If the primacord manifest means what it appears to mean, the desalination plant is wired for demolition, with the firing point in the control blockhouse on the lagoon's north arm.
complications.mechanicalEffect: UNCONFIRMED — basis: fence manifest, 11 days old. If real: charges arm 45 minutes after any perimeter alarm; the blockhouse must be taken before arming completes or the secondary objective fails on a band commander's order.

decisionPoints.name: The Exclusive
decisionPoints.context: The rim-port fence offers exclusivity — his manifest feed sold to your unit alone — for 12,000 C-bills, payable in actual currency the realm will not provide. The unit's own funds, the unit's own risk, against a promise from a man whose business model is selling the same thing twice.

options.title: Buy the Exclusive
advantages: If honored, the band's purchasing trail goes dark to them and bright to you — supply schedule, charge purchases, DropShip parts orders
The receipt itself is evidence: if he double-sells, the merc review boards treat documented exclusivity breach as actionable, and he knows it
disadvantages: 12,000 C-bills of unit money on a handshake with a professional double-dealer
The realm's liaison notes the unit doing private business with the rim's grey market, in the report that follows the unit home
options.consequence: The intelligence flow is the best available on the circuit — and its reliability is a bet placed on a fence's fear of paperwork, which has held before and broken before.

costs.resource: unit funds, not contract funds — the realm pays in kind only
costs.risk: a handshake with a professional double-dealer, noted in the liaison's report that follows the unit home

options.title: Feed Him a False Plan
advantages: Costs nothing but craft: buy the standard feed, let slip a windward assault date 4 days late, and see where the band digs in
If he sells it, the Red Ledger fortifies the wrong shore and the real assault meets half a defense
disadvantages: If he does not sell it, the unit has spent its credibility with the only fence on the circuit for nothing
Disinformation discovered is a grudge: the next manifest the unit buys anywhere on the rim may come pre-poisoned
options.consequence: The approach becomes a test of the leak as much as an attack — decisive advantage if the leak is real, a burned relationship and an alert enemy if it is not.

costs.resource: the standard feed's purchase price plus the unit's credibility with the only manifest fence on the circuit, staked
costs.risk: disinformation discovered is a grudge — the next manifest bought anywhere on the rim may arrive pre-poisoned

options.title: Report Him to the Realm's Intelligence
advantages: The liaison's trust rises measurably, and the realm's counterintelligence owes the unit a favor it can collect later
Removes the band's intelligence source at the same stroke — they shop at the same counter
disadvantages: The fence vanishes within 5 days of the report, and the rim's grey market closes to the unit for the contract's duration
All future intelligence arrives through official channels: twice the age, half the texture
options.consequence: Both sides of the war go blind, and the side with the prepared defensive position needs intelligence less.

costs.resource: the rim's grey market, closed to the unit for the contract's duration
costs.risk: all future intelligence via official channels — twice the age, half the texture, and the dug-in side needs it less

decisionPoints.name: Low Tide
decisionPoints.context: The Combs cross only at low water. Two windows differ in everything: depth, light, duration. A third option avoids the shelf entirely and borrows civilians to do it.

options.title: Spring Low, 04:40
advantages: Best depth and the longest window — 100 minutes, full force across in darkness
Shore batteries' pressed crews shoot worst at night, and they shoot badly to start with
disadvantages: Night footing on coral: footing checks one step harder, and a 'Mech down in the channel floods before the next window
The whole force is on the shelf when the window closes — there is no halfway
options.consequence: Maximum force delivered in darkness against a defense that may or may not have bought the date; the tide table is public knowledge and the band can read a moon as well as anyone.

costs.resource: the whole force committed to the shelf inside one 100-minute window — there is no halfway
costs.risk: night footing one step harder; a 'Mech down in a channel floods before the next window

options.title: Neap Low, 14:10
advantages: Daylight footing: checks at standard difficulty, engineering recovery possible inside the window
Aerospace and battery-counterfire spotting actually function
disadvantages: 60-minute window, shallower margins, and every shore battery sees the entire approach
Daylight crossing under observed fire is exactly the engagement the pressed crews cannot miss forever
options.consequence: A safer shelf and a far more dangerous sky: the crossing succeeds on suppression discipline or becomes a gunnery exercise for the defenders.

costs.resource: a 60-minute window with shallower margins — the shortest crossing budget on the tide table
costs.risk: every shore battery observes the entire daylight approach; pressed crews cannot miss forever

options.title: The Fishermen's Door
advantages: local boat crews — kin to the pressed gunners — will run a commando element to the windward breakwater for pay and the chance of their cousins back
Lands behind the batteries entirely; the Combs become a feint
disadvantages: Civilian boats and civilian nerve in the assault chain; one challenge on the water unravels it
The liaison must countersign civilian hazard pay, and the 6-hour delay applies while the tide tables keep turning
options.consequence: The batteries are taken from behind by people their crews will not fire on — if the boats hold their nerve and the paperwork clears before the weather turns.

costs.resource: civilian hazard pay for the local boat crews, liaison-countersigned — the 6-hour approval delay spends while the tide tables keep turning
costs.risk: civilian boats and civilian nerve in the assault chain; one challenge on the water unravels it

entries.event: Shore battery fires illumination over the Combs; lair alarm; band fighters to the causeways.
5 ready band 'Mechs man the lagoon causeways; both PPC heavies anchor the main channel.
DropShip 1 begins pre-flight; loading parties start moving registry bonds and prize cargo.
Scuttle teams dispatched to the desalination plant; arming sequence begins if charges are real.
Plant charges armed. Control blockhouse firing point live from this moment.
DropShip 1 lift-capable with leadership and bonds aboard.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Control blockhouse secured by T+0:45 or the priced asset is one switch from rubble, and the contract converts to bounty-only terms at a 60 percent revenue cut. The liaison will record the exact minute the blockhouse fell. Plan to be early.

opforSketch.composition: 9 pirate BattleMechs (Green-to-Regular, salvage mix, 2 PPC-armed heavies as causeway anchors), 2 DropShips (1 likely flight-capable — UNCONFIRMED), 4 shore batteries with pressed crews at -1, 60-80 fighters. Generator should keep the heavies static on the causeways and the rest mobile in the lagoon's interior.
opforSketch.behavior: The Red Ledger defends the lagoon mouth, trades pressed crews and outer works for time, and scuttles before surrendering assets. Leadership under {NPC:opfor-commander} lifts the moment the inner lagoon is breached. They have sold prizes through paperwork for years: expect them to negotiate, stall, and lie with documents as fluently as with guns.

forks.name: OPERATION FRESH WATER
forks.trigger: Band broken, plant intact, blockhouse taken before arming.
forks.consequence: The realm exercises its 12-month garrison option at improved rates, and the liaison's report — read aloud in district council — opens contracts previously closed to outside units. Payment-in-kind converts to a standing supply line.

forks.name: OPERATION SALTED EARTH
forks.trigger: Plant destroyed, or band escapes with both DropShips.
forks.consequence: The district refuses the payment-in-kind balance, citing the schedule's plain text. The unit's homeward fuel becomes a negotiation conducted from weakness, on a rim where the only other fuel seller is the fence who may have caused the problem.

forks.name: OPERATION DOUBLE ENTRY
forks.trigger: Post-action evidence that the fence sold the unit's real approach to the band.
forks.consequence: The question becomes who else he sold, and when. The unit hunts the leak back through the rim port's grey market with the liaison auditing every C-bill of the hunt — and the answer implicates a customer list long enough to be its own campaign.

storyElementSeed: The liaison officer initials each line of the fuel manifest with a steel pen, unhurried, while the loadmaster stands holding the hose clamp; neither speaks, because the pen is the actual chain of command and both of them know it.

periphery/pirate.objectives.secondary: The desal plant runs or the district drinks brine — take it whole. Bounty money spends once; a working water plant is rent forever, and whoever hands the realm its plant back gets remembered past the next drought.

resourceGates.lackingText: The exclusivity fee is actual currency the realm will not provide. Below 12,000 C-bills of unit funds the option is closed; the standard feed is the only counter open.

phases.name: THE COUNTER
phases.lead: Phase one is fought at a manifest counter on the rim port and at a liaison's folding desk: what the unit buys, what the band learns, and what the realm countersigns. Every plan that leaves this phase must survive being sold.

dataBlock.Intelligence age: band picture 16 days old, confidence LOW; the primacord manifest is 11 days old and UNCONFIRMED
dataBlock.Exclusivity: 12,000 C-bills, unit funds only — the realm pays in kind and the fence does not take fuel
dataBlock.Liaison signature: required above 1 fuel load; 6-hour delay; unsigned emergency spend runs a 30 percent breach risk at double value

phases.protocol: Spending requests go to {NPC:employer-contact} in writing, 1 page, costed in kind, submitted before 18:00 for a midnight signature. Verbal authorizations do not exist. The liaison's standing phrase is 'the realm pays on paper,' and the campaign learns to plan around the sentence rather than against it.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The difference between intelligence that is wrong and intelligence that is sold: which of the 16-day-old numbers the band would most want the unit to keep believing.

phases.name: THE COMBS
phases.lead: Eleven kilometers of coral shelf, 2 tide windows a day, a typhoon every week or so. The crossing is a timetable problem the enemy gets to shoot at.

dataBlock.Tide table: spring low 04:40 local, 100-minute window; neap low 14:10, 60 minutes; depth 0.4-1.1 meters at low water
dataBlock.Mobility: 'Mechs at walking speed with footing checks; hovercraft run free; tracked and wheeled do not cross
dataBlock.Typhoon: 1-in-3 per 72-hour window; the Combs close under 3 meters of surge and storms end in 12-36 hours

routes.name: Route COMB
routes.desc: the shelf's coral spine, 0.4-0.6 meters at low water, the firmest footing on the crossing
routes.tradeoff: Standard footing checks only; the final 3 kilometers run straight up battery 2's registered arc.

routes.name: Route TROUGH
routes.desc: the northern sand channel, 0.9-1.1 meters, hull-down to 'Mech knees
routes.tradeoff: Outside the batteries' registered arcs (UNCONFIRMED — basis: fishermen's sketch, 9 days old); footing checks one step harder the whole way.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The next 10 days of tide windows laid against the typhoon odds — which windows exist on paper only, and which one the weather will eat.

phases.name: THE LAGOON
phases.lead: Past the shelf the fight narrows to one building: the control blockhouse on the north arm, firing point for charges that may or may not exist, on a 45-minute arming clock that starts with the first alarm. Plan as if the primacord manifest is true — the alternative only plans for embarrassment.

dataBlock.Blockhouse: lagoon north arm; if the charges are real they arm at T+0:45 from perimeter alarm
dataBlock.Causeway anchors: 2 PPC-armed heavies static on the main channel
dataBlock.DropShip 1: lift-capable T+0:55 with leadership and the registry bonds aboard

phases.protocol: First contact with each shore battery opens with a loudhailer call in the local coastal dialect — NETS DOWN — carried ahead of the assault to the pressed crews' kin by the local boat families. On the call, crews abandon mounts seaward, hands on heads, and wade for the marked sandbar. A battery still firing 60 seconds after the call is treated as guarded: suppress the guards, not the gun.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The order nobody wants to pre-write: what the assault does at minute 44 if the blockhouse still holds — written anyway, signed, and put where the liaison can read it.

assetDetails.detail: The contract's priced asset: the payment-in-kind schedule is calculated on its return to service, and wreckage converts the deal to bounty-only at a 60 percent cut. The realm's district archive holds the original Star League as-built drawings and can produce them on 48 hours' notice — nobody has asked yet.

Fishermen taken in the band's last raid, kin to the local boat crews, serving under guard and aiming badly on purpose. 3 or more dead halves the bonus payout and closes a future contract with the realm — the district command reads casualty lists aloud in council.
Audits like a calling and signs nothing unread twice. The liaison's report follows the unit home whatever happens at the atoll; what goes into it is a campaign objective no annex names.

title: OPERATION LAST CISTERN
skeleton: a relief escort that cannot reach every dying settlement in time becomes the triage authority, choosing whom to save first while a toll-taking warlord prices the only road and the desert's flash floods price delay
inspiration: famine-relief convoys run past warlord checkpoints in a collapsing dry country — the Somalia aid corridors, 1992
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. It is the third dry year in the basin, and the basin has run out of slack. Three population centers remain. The walled city of Qedem holds 31,000 people; its cisterns run completely dry at H+78, and that reading is the water board's own gauge, so it is solid. The Tarsh mine camp holds 4,200 people, its pumps failing and its shafts flooding upward toward the working levels. The Bani wells confederacy is roughly 6,000 people across 14 nomad camps, losing 6 to 9 people a day to thirst and the diseases that follow it — but that count is 8 days old and unconfirmed, relayed from camp riders through {NPC:intel-source}, so treat it as rough. {EMPLOYER} — an offworld merchant combine with a charity mandate that its lawyers wrote and at least its junior partners genuinely mean — has put together a relief convoy: 22 trucks, 60 tons of grain, a refrigerated vaccine chest, and 2 truck-mounted fusion-powered water crackers, each able to keep 20,000 people alive indefinitely once it is set up. Your unit is the escort, which also makes your unit the one that decides who gets saved first. The route works against you: the Shattered Palms are a 60-kilometer network of braided dry riverbeds (wadis), and the graded track through them is the only way into the basin. Off that track, soft sand bogs down a loaded truck within 400 meters. Ridge spurs overlook the route at 11 separate points, and a warlord who used to be the basin's tax collector now controls the road: {NPC:opfor-commander}, leading an estimated 200 riders, 11 technicals, and 1 to 3 BattleMechs. Those numbers come from caravan survivors and are 19 days old, so the 'Mech count especially could be higher. His business is the toll. He does not want the convoy destroyed, because destroyed convoys stop coming; he wants 30 percent of the cargo, and he wants it established that 30 percent is the price of using his roads. Storm cells cross the basin every 8 to 12 days and flash-flood the wadis with only 90 minutes of warning — meaning the convoy can actually drown in the desert. Each population center is a 30-hour drive from the route's central fork, and the two crackers cannot cover all three. There is no clean answer to the math. The convoy carries the entire survival margin for {WORLD}'s basin, and everyone on the road — the emir's guards, the mine bosses, the camp riders, the warlord, and you — has already done the same division and come up with a different answer about who matters most.

objectives.primary: Deliver both water crackers and at least 80 percent of cargo to a minimum of 2 of the 3 population centers before their respective failure points.
objectives.secondary: Concede zero cargo to toll demands — every concession sets the precedent the next convoy pays for.
objectives.bonus: Broker a wells-truce: Bani riders hired as paid convoy scouts, converting the basin's best terrain intelligence from threat to asset.

complications.name: Heat Doctrine
complications.text: Daytime basin temperatures hold above 45 degrees. Truck engines derate, crews wilt, and BattleMech heat curves climb before a single weapon fires. The convoy moves at night or it cooks.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Daylight operations: +2 heat to all 'Mech activity, truck speed capped at 20 kph, crew fatigue accumulates. Usable night movement window: 9 hours per local day.

complications.name: Flash Flood
complications.text: A storm cell over the highlands sends a flood down the wadis with 90 minutes of warning from the spotters' barometers. A loaded convoy caught between the high banks loses vehicles to the rushing water — in a place with no water to spare, the flood is what kills.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Storm roll each 8-12 days. On warning: 90-minute clock to reach high bank; trucks move at half speed in soft sand. Vehicles caught in the braid at zero: swept, cargo lost, 1d3 crew casualties per truck.

complications.name: Tax Precedent
complications.text: The warlord's demands are a market test. Every concession reprices the route — and word of what the convoy paid travels ahead of it, to the next ridge and the next demand.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each negotiated concession raises every subsequent demand by 25 percent of base, cumulative, and is known at all later checkpoints. The secondary objective fails on the first concession.

complications.name: Cholera at the Qedem Gate
complications.text: The city's gate quarter is reporting rice-water cases. The emir's guards run a quarantine line with more zeal than training, and every convoy entry stalls in the crush of people who want out.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each Qedem entry or exit: 3-hour quarantine delay. Medical personnel can cut this to 1 hour and reduce gate-crowd unrest one step per visit.

decisionPoints.name: Three Cisterns, One Road
decisionPoints.context: From the hub fork, each center is a 30-hour leg and the legs do not combine. The order of delivery is the order of who waits, and one of the three numbers at the top of the brief is a countdown.

options.title: Qedem First
advantages: 31,000 people and a cistern gauge reading H+78 — the largest number and the hardest deadline
The city's hinterland is the warlord's recruiting pool; a fed Qedem starves his cause at the root
disadvantages: The emir taxes incoming relief 30 percent for 'distribution', and his guards skim above that
The mine camp's pumps and the Bani's children are spending the same 30 hours
options.consequence: The most lives reached soonest, a third of the cargo lost to the gate before it reaches a single cistern, and the basin learns the convoy can be taxed by anyone with a wall.

costs.resource: emir's gate tax: 30 percent of delivered relief for distribution, plus guard skim above it
costs.risk: the Tarsh pumps and the Bani camps spend the same 30 hours waiting

options.title: Tarsh First
advantages: The mine's shops and fuel point keep the convoy itself running — self-sufficiency for the remaining legs
Smallest population, fastest emplacement: a cracker running at Tarsh inside 36 hours, miners paying in diesel and spare parts
disadvantages: 4,200 people served first while 31,000 count down — the optics are exactly what they look like
{EMPLOYER}'s charity mandate was drafted around the city, and the junior partners will read the sequencing aloud
options.consequence: The convoy can now keep itself running for the rest of the operation, but at a moral cost; Qedem's water margin shrinks to a matter of hours, and the emir's version of events reaches the combine before yours does.

costs.resource: {EMPLOYER}'s charity-mandate standing — 4,200 served first while 31,000 count down against an H+78 gauge
costs.risk: Qedem's margin shrinks to hours and the emir's version of events reaches the combine first

options.title: Bani Wells First
advantages: The camps are dying quietly at a rate the other ledgers ignore, and they hold every wadi junction in the braid
A wells-truce converts 14 camps of riders into the convoy's eyes — safe passage for all later legs, and the bonus objective in hand
disadvantages: Fewest people by count, and the cold arithmetic of the mandate says count
30 hours spent on the smallest number while the largest number's gauge falls
options.consequence: The desert's owners become the convoy's allies and every subsequent leg runs under friendly observation — purchased at the cost of being able to say the biggest number came first.

costs.resource: 30 hours spent on the smallest number while the largest number's gauge falls
costs.risk: the mandate's cold arithmetic says count, and the count came last — the combine reads the sequencing aloud

decisionPoints.name: The Rear Third
decisionPoints.context: At the Palm Gate narrows the warlord's riders cut off the trailing 7 trucks — drivers hired at Qedem, grain and one cracker aboard — and hold them at rifle point on the low ground while the storm spotters watch the highlands and the envoy walks forward under white cloth.

options.title: Turn and Fight
advantages: Full escort against riders and technicals is a short, one-sided engagement on open ground
Demonstrates the route cannot be cut, which is the only message the warlord respects at full volume
disadvantages: 12+ hours lost to the engagement and recovery against Qedem's falling gauge
The trucks sit in the kill zone while it happens, and riflemen at zero range do not need to win to cost
options.consequence: The toll is broken as a practice, but the schedule pays the price — the Qedem delivery has to absorb the lost half-day, and the cistern gauge keeps falling no matter what.

costs.resource: 12-plus hours of Qedem's falling cistern gauge, spent on the engagement and recovery
costs.risk: 7 trucks sit in the kill zone while it happens — riflemen at zero range do not need to win to cost

options.title: Pay in Grain
advantages: 4 trucks of grain buys the rear third free in 40 minutes, no casualties, schedule intact
The warlord's riders eat, which is — say it plainly — also relief
disadvantages: The tax precedent complication triggers at full force: +25 percent at every remaining checkpoint, forever
The secondary objective fails and {EMPLOYER}'s next convoy inherits the price list
options.consequence: Today's mission arrives nearly whole and every future mission on this road is born owing 30 percent — the schedule was saved by mortgaging the route.

costs.resource: 4 trucks of grain, plus every later checkpoint demand raised 25 percent of base, cumulative and known down the road
costs.risk: the secondary objective fails on the first concession — the next convoy inherits the price list

options.title: Drive On
advantages: The lead element and both crackers reach the hub fork on schedule, untouched
Refusing to stop denies the warlord both toll and engagement — his ambush closes on nothing of value he can hold
disadvantages: 7 drivers hired at Qedem, abandoned with their trucks at rifle point, and the city will hear it before the convoy arrives
The grain in those trucks is 30 percent of the food relief
options.consequence: The crackers — the things that cannot be replaced — arrive intact, and the convoy enters Qedem as the outfit that left the city's own drivers in the narrows; the gate crowd's arithmetic on that is not in your favor.

costs.resource: 7 trucks, 7 Qedem-hired drivers, and 30 percent of the food relief, left at rifle point
costs.risk: the gate crowd's arithmetic on abandoned city drivers — and Qedem hears it before the convoy arrives

entries.event: Outrider contact: lead vehicle disabled by a command mine at the Palm Gate narrows. Convoy alarm.
Technicals demonstrate on the south ridge — visible, not firing. The display is the message.
1 raider BattleMech shows itself on the overwatch spur, weapons cold. Posture, not attack.
Envoy rides in under white cloth with the toll demand: 30 percent of cargo, counted on the spot.
If refused without counter-offer, harassing fire begins on the rear third — tires, radiators, nothing human yet.
Storm cell flagged at dawn reaches the highlands; flash-flood warning window opens for the braid.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The convoy clears the Palm Gate narrows by T+4:00 or it negotiates inside a flood channel with 90 minutes of warning and 22 loaded trucks at half speed in soft sand. The warlord knows the weather as well as the spotters do. He picked this spot because the desert charges its own toll, and his opening offer is cheaper.

opforSketch.composition: 150-220 riders operating in bands of 20-40, 8-12 armed technicals, 1-3 BattleMechs (Green pilots, ammunition-poor — they posture more than they fight), Veteran core bodyguard around {NPC:opfor-commander}. Generator should weight mobility and numbers over armor, with the 'Mechs as theater pieces that become real if cornered.
opforSketch.behavior: Extortion first, attrition second, never decisive engagement. Bands break contact at roughly 25 percent casualties. The warlord preserves the route's value above any single prize — he will burn a checkpoint's worth of riders to save the toll as an institution, and not one rider more.

forks.name: OPERATION GREEN FLAG
forks.trigger: 2+ deliveries made before failure points, zero toll concessions.
forks.consequence: The combine funds a standing escort contract for the basin route, and the Bani scouts ride under the unit's banner — the wells-truce becomes the region's first functioning security arrangement since the rains stopped, with the unit as its spine.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY BOWL
forks.trigger: Qedem's cisterns fail before delivery.
forks.consequence: The city opens its gates to the warlord, who arrives with water he taxed from earlier caravans and a long memory of who refused him. The mission becomes a 31,000-person evacuation triage under the guns of the basin's new ruler, and the combine's charity effort turns into a list of who it failed.

forks.name: OPERATION TITHE ROAD
forks.trigger: Deliveries made but toll paid at any checkpoint.
forks.consequence: Every road in the district now has a published price, and the precedent compounds at 25 percent per checkpoint. Follow-on relief contracts price the toll into their budgets, which means less cargo per convoy, which means the next triage starts harder than this one did.

storyElementSeed: A driver pours exactly one cup from the radiator can, drinks half, and pours the rest back through a folded cloth; the cloth hangs on the mirror to dry, because tomorrow it does the same job again.

is-marik.objectives.secondary: No concessions to toll demands — the assembly's relief appropriation passed on the explicit assurance that not one gram feeds a warlord, and the opposition benches are waiting for the receipt that proves otherwise.

phases.name: THE BRAID
phases.lead: Sixty kilometers of braided wadi between the coast road and the hub fork, moved at night in 9-hour windows, under 11 ridge spurs that each hold a watcher. The convoy's speed is set by its slowest loaded truck and its survival by the storm spotters' barometers.

dataBlock.March table: night window 9 hours; 35 kph on the graded line, half that in soft sand, 20 kph cap in daylight heat
dataBlock.Flood warning: 90 minutes from the barometer drop to water in the braid
dataBlock.Overwatch: 11 ridge spurs flank the graded line; assume every spur reports
dataBlock.Stowage: crackers sealed on dedicated transporters; vaccine chest rides the command truck

phases.protocol: Approach to any Bani camp: halt at 400 meters, lights doused, lead engine off, 3 slow flashes from a hand lamp — then wait for a rider to come to you. Entering camp ground unannounced is answered with rifles, and correctly so. If a wells-truce happens, it begins with the convoy being the first outfit this year to stop at 400 meters.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The load plan as triage: which trucks carry the crackers, which the vaccine chest, and the order the column abandons vehicles if the braid floods at minute 60 of 90.

phases.name: PALM GATE
phases.lead: The warlord's toll is a negotiation staged as an ambush: a mined lead vehicle, technicals posing on the ridge, an envoy under white cloth, and a storm cell due at T+4:00. He wants 30 percent and a precedent; the desert wants the whole convoy.

dataBlock.The demand: 30 percent of cargo, counted on the spot, delivered by envoy at T+0:45
dataBlock.Escalation: harassing fire on the rear third from T+1:30 if refused without counter-offer — tires and radiators first
dataBlock.The desert's clock: flood window opens T+4:00; 22 loaded trucks make half speed in soft sand
dataBlock.His arithmetic: destroyed convoys stop coming; his bands break contact at roughly 25 percent casualties

phases.protocol: Parley form: the envoy rides in under white cloth and is met by 2, on foot, unhelmeted, between the lines, weapons slung. Counter-offers are made once and kept — a retracted offer reads as weakness, a refused parley as insult, and both reprice the road. The white cloth protects the envoy in both directions; whoever breaks it first owns the wells' verdict.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The half-day a fight here costs against Qedem's falling gauge — the sum done in the open, where the envoy can watch it being done.

phases.name: THE LEGS
phases.lead: From the hub fork, three 30-hour legs that do not combine. The crackers cannot be everywhere; the delivery order is the triage, and every party in the basin has already done the division and gotten a different remainder.

dataBlock.Qedem: 31,000 people; cisterns dead-empty at H+78 (confidence HIGH); 30 percent gate tax plus guard skim; 3-hour cholera quarantine per entry
dataBlock.Tarsh: 4,200; pumps failing, shafts flooding upward; the only machine shops and fuel point in the basin
dataBlock.Bani: roughly 6,000 across 14 camps; 6-9 deaths per day (confidence LOW); holders of every wadi junction
dataBlock.Emplacement: a cracker reaches first water 36 hours after reaching a prepared site, and serves 20,000 indefinitely

sidebarKernel.kernel: Rice-water cases at the Qedem gate quarter: what the vaccine chest covers and what it does not, and the 2 hours of quarantine a medic's presence buys back per entry.

assetDetails.detail: Fusion-powered, 20,000 people each, indefinitely — and irreplaceable within the combine's charity budget for years. Each rides a dedicated transporter that cannot ford soft sand; a bogged cracker is a besieged cracker within a day. Emplacement needs level rock, 36 hours, and a guard that stays after the convoy leaves.

One chest, no spare cooling charge in the basin: it holds temperature only if it stays sealed between camps, and the Qedem quarantine line will want it opened for inspection. The medical officer carries the authority to refuse — using that authority at a gate crowded with sick people is its own decision point.

Hired at the gate for grain wages; they know the braid better than the escort, and the warlord's riders know their families. They will drive through anything except a fight against their own city's tax collectors — brief them last, count them at every halt.

title: OPERATION SALT MERIDIAN
skeleton: a politically hobbled relief column must beat an irreversible engineering deadline across a mined salt causeway it cannot leave, hunted by a stay-behind force built entirely light enough to leave it, while a legislative rider bars its heavy 'Mechs from the city it is saving
inspiration: a clearance-and-relief drive down a single mined causeway under contested command — the Walcheren causeway crossing, 1944
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. Nineteen days ago a {TARGET_FACTION} raiding force burned the basin's grain terminal and punched holes in the cooling system of its fusion power station before withdrawing offworld — most of it withdrew, and the provincial assembly has been arguing about the part that stayed ever since. The station is running at 40 percent on its backup heat exchangers, and the chief engineer projects it will be forced to shut down — a scram — at H+91, counted from your column's departure. She has staked her career on that number, so treat it as firm. When the station scrams, the basin's water pumps stop. 340,000 people live in the basin on {WORLD}, already rationed to 1,900 kilocalories a day. The assembly approved federal relief by a vote of 14 to 9, but only with Rider 6 attached to win over the city delegates: federal BattleMechs may not enter the city limits under any circumstances. The delegates say they remember a garrison incident seven years ago, and at this point the reason no longer matters — the rule stands. Your column carries the replacement cooling system (3 transporter loads) and food. The route is the Causeway: 31 kilometers of elevated road across the Meridian Salt, a thin crust over brine mud that breaks under anything heavier than 35 tons within 200 meters of leaving the roadbed. That is the core terrain problem, and the enemy has studied it more carefully than the assembly has. {TARGET_FACTION} engineers mined the causeway as they withdrew — an estimated 47 charges. That figure is 6 days old, from {NPC:intel-source}, and rated fair. A {TARGET_FACTION} stay-behind force operates from the salt flats: 4 light jump-capable 'Mechs, every one of them 35 tons or under, plus 2 jump-infantry platoons. That strength is unconfirmed, pieced together from track surveys and 2 contact reports, so it could be larger. Pay attention to that tonnage choice: they deliberately picked machines light enough for the crust to bear, so they can leave the road and you cannot. Command is divided: the Duchy militia claims escort authority inside the basin, the federal column holds it on the causeway, and Rider 6 hands the militia the final 4 kilometers no matter what. An assembly observer ({NPC:employer-contact}) rides with the column and files a report every night. Refugees walking out of the basin have already taken over one of the causeway's two lanes. The column moves in 6-hour slots, one convoy per slot, and the scram countdown burns through those slots whether the column uses them or not.

objectives.primary: Deliver all 3 cooling-train transporter loads to the basin's fusion station before scram at H+91.
objectives.secondary: Sustain 18 food convoy slots over 10 days without losing a slot to mines, raids, or politics.
objectives.bonus: Take a {TARGET_FACTION} stay-behind prisoner — the assembly wants documented proof of mine-laying against civilian infrastructure for the parliamentary record.

complications.name: Mine Belt
complications.text: 47 charges, give or take, distributed along 31 kilometers with an engineer's eye for chokepoints and pylon footings. Sweeping is slow, certain, and the only way; not sweeping is fast until it is suddenly very slow.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Engineering vehicles clear 800 meters per hour. Convoys on unswept causeway: lead-vehicle mine check per kilometer. A transporter mine-kill blocks the lane for 3 hours minimum.

complications.name: Refugee Counterflow
complications.text: The second lane belongs to people walking out of the basin with what they can carry. Any 'Mech moving above walking pace on the causeway scatters them — over the rail, onto the salt, into the column's path.
complications.mechanicalEffect: One lane only for column traffic. 'Mech movement above Walking: refugee casualty roll, and any civilian casualty triggers the observer's incident report (see Rider 6) plus a 12-hour militia stand-down for inquiry.

complications.name: Rider 6
complications.text: Federal BattleMechs inside city limits constitute a political incident regardless of cause — pursuit, medevac, riot response, all of it. The observer's nightly file goes to 23 assembly members, 9 of whom voted no.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any federal 'Mech crossing the city limit: relief authorization suspended 72 hours pending inquiry while all clocks continue. The final 4 kilometers of every delivery are militia-escorted only.

complications.name: Brine Bog
complications.text: Off the causeway, the Meridian Salt holds 35 tons and breaks under more. The stay-behind lance is built entirely under that line. The column's combat power mostly is not.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Units above 35 tons leaving the causeway: bog check per 200 meters, sinking is mission-kill until heavy recovery. Units 35 tons and under move on the salt at one movement class slower, no bog check on crust marked stable.

decisionPoints.name: Sequencing the Slots
decisionPoints.context: The causeway allows one convoy per 6-hour slot. The cooling system needs 3 slots; the food needs 18. The scram countdown reads H+91, and the city's gates already have angry bread queues forming.

options.title: Cooling Train First
advantages: The station is the basin's water, and the water is everything else — secure the deadline that cannot be argued with
3 consecutive slots gets the train delivered with 60+ hours of margin against H+91
disadvantages: The city eats 1,900 kilocalories for 3 more days while transporters roll past the bread queues
Gate-riot probability climbs with every food slot deferred, and the militia answers riots its own way
options.consequence: The engineering deadline is beaten with room to spare; the political deadline arrives early, at the gates, on camera, in the observer's nightly file.

costs.resource: 3 more days of 1,900-kilocalorie queues while transporters roll past the bread lines
costs.risk: gate-riot probability climbs with every deferred food slot, and the militia answers riots its own way

options.title: Food First
advantages: Queues shorten, the gate quarter calms, and the militia's riot problem becomes a distribution problem
The urban delegates who hung Rider 6 on the bill see relief with their names on it
disadvantages: The cooling train's margin shrinks to 19 hours — one mined transporter, one lost slot, and the station scrams
The chief engineer's projection has error bars and they do not point in the helpful direction
options.consequence: The city is fed and quiet, but the whole mission now rests on three late slots running clean through a mine belt. It is a bet that the hardest part goes perfectly at the very end, after a week in which little else has.

costs.resource: the cooling train's delivery margin, cut to 19 hours against the H+91 scram
costs.risk: one mined transporter, one lost slot, and the station scrams — the error bars do not point the helpful way

options.title: Split the Column
advantages: Cooling train on slots 1 and 3, food on slot 2 — both clocks serviced, neither abandoned
Flexibility to re-sequence if a slot is lost
disadvantages: Escort strength divides across the causeway's length, and the stay-behind lance gets a menu instead of a target
Recovery assets can be in one place; a mine strike at the wrong slot strands the train mid-causeway
options.consequence: The politically survivable choice and the tactically thinnest one: every convoy is a little under-escorted, and the {TARGET_FACTION} commander on the salt gets to choose which one that matters for.

costs.resource: escort strength, divided across 31 kilometers of causeway; recovery assets can be in one place only
costs.risk: every convoy a little under-escorted — the stay-behind commander picks which one that matters for

decisionPoints.name: Pylon 19
decisionPoints.context: The stay-behinds hit the militia checkpoint at Pylon 19 and withdraw into the pans — slowly, visibly, at a pace calculated to be followed. The militia colonel demands pursuit. The observer is watching. The clock is running.

options.title: Pursue onto the Salt
advantages: Only the column's 2 lightest machines can follow, but a kill or capture ends the harassment campaign at its source
Taking a stay-behind prisoner alive during the pursuit completes the bonus objective directly
disadvantages: 2 'Mechs against 4 on ground the enemy chose and surveyed — the bait is not subtle and does not need to be
While the pursuit runs, the causeway's escort is short exactly those 2 machines
options.consequence: The enemy finally gets the engagement it has been purchasing checkpoint by checkpoint; whether it bought a defeat or a double kill depends on two pilots and ground truth nobody on the causeway can see.

costs.resource: the causeway escort, short its 2 lightest machines for the pursuit's duration
costs.risk: 2 against 4 on ground the enemy chose and surveyed — the bait is not subtle and does not need to be

options.title: Screen and Continue
advantages: The slots keep moving and the scram clock keeps being beaten
No federal machine leaves the road; Rider 6 stays unbreached; the observer's file stays boring
disadvantages: The stay-behind lance remains in being, and every subsequent slot runs 25 percent slower under threat posture
The militia colonel files a formal protest of federal timidity — with the same assembly that holds the authorization
options.consequence: Tactically clean and politically corrosive: the column trades a fight it might win for a friction it definitely keeps, and the enemy learns the convoys will never come off the road for anything.

costs.resource: every subsequent slot runs 25 percent slower under threat posture — paid against the H+91 clock
costs.risk: a formal militia protest of federal timidity, filed with the assembly that holds the authorization

options.title: Hand the Militia the Pursuit
advantages: The militia's hover platoon is the one asset on the causeway the salt cannot bog
Duchy troops taking the fight forward repairs the command friction in front of the observer
disadvantages: The militia colonel sets a condition: operational subordination of the federal escort for the duration — a precedent the duchy will cite for the rest of the relief
Hover infantry against jump 'Mechs needs the engagement to go exactly as briefed, and the colonel writes brave briefs
options.consequence: The pursuit happens under a flag the assembly cannot object to, commanded by an officer with a point to prove, and whatever it costs, the duchy owns the result — including the version where it needs rescuing on ground your tonnage cannot enter.

costs.resource: operational subordination of the federal escort for the duration — a precedent the duchy will cite for the rest of the relief
costs.risk: hover infantry against jump 'Mechs under an officer who writes brave briefs; rescue means ground your tonnage cannot enter

entries.event: Lead transporter mined at kilometer 12. Column halts in herringbone; alarm to all stations.
Refugee counterflow compresses at the blockage; both directions of the causeway lock within 15 minutes.
Stay-behind LRM harassment opens from the pans, 2 'Mechs displacing between salt hummocks after each volley.
Militia hover section arrives from Pylon 22; command of the response is immediately in dispute.
Heavy crane vehicle can reach kilometer 12 from the city end — if the refugee lane is opened, which is a decision with a casualty risk attached.
Stay-behinds break contact on doctrine: 90-120 minute raids, never decisive engagement.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The mined transporter recovered or pushed off the causeway by T+3:00. Each causeway hour lost burns delivery slots the schedule cannot mint more of, and the station scram at H+91 does not attend assembly sessions, read protests, or negotiate. The enemy's entire campaign is the arithmetic of your lost hours; deny them the hours.

opforSketch.composition: {TARGET_FACTION} stay-behind force: 4 light BattleMechs (30-35 tons, jump-capable, Veteran — picked crews left behind on purpose), 2 jump infantry platoons, 1 supply cache in the pans (location UNCONFIRMED). Generator should select fast, jump-capable lights with LRM or harassment loadouts, all under the 35-ton crust line.
opforSketch.behavior: Harass-and-fade against the slot schedule: mine strikes, checkpoint raids, 90-120 minute engagements, never decisive contact. Targets transporters and engineering vehicles over combat units. The commander's object is not victory but expense — making League relief politically and materially costlier than the raid that caused it.

forks.name: OPERATION RESTORED CURRENT
forks.trigger: Cooling train delivered before H+91 and 18 food slots sustained.
forks.consequence: The station holds, the basin drinks, and the assembly votes thanks 19 to 4. The column's conduct under Rider 6 becomes the precedent cited in the next 3 relief authorizations, and the unit is requested by name in committee — which in the League is both a salary and a leash.

forks.name: OPERATION BLACKOUT MARCH
forks.trigger: Station scrams at H+91 with the cooling train undelivered.
forks.consequence: The pumps stop. The mission converts to a 340,000-person staged water-haul and evacuation under riot conditions, with the militia and the federal column blaming each other in front of an observer whose nightly file has become the most-read document in the province.

forks.name: OPERATION RIDER SIX
forks.trigger: Any federal BattleMech crosses city limits, for any reason.
forks.consequence: The assembly suspends the relief authorization for 72 hours pending inquiry while every clock keeps running. The column operates the causeway under militia escort only, the stay-behinds enjoy the most productive three days of their campaign, and the inquiry's first witness is the observer.

storyElementSeed: An engineering sergeant chalks a number on each causeway pylon as the sweep team clears it, then initials the chalk; nineteen pylons back the chalk carries a different team's initials, and the sergeant walks back through the cold to check their work anyway.

merc.objectives.primary: Deliver the cooling train before the H+91 scram — that line item is the contract. The 18 food slots are the option clause. Rider 6 is the employer's politics, but the breach penalty lands in your ledger: keep the 'Mechs outside the line on the map, whatever is burning inside it.

phases.name: THE SWEEP
phases.lead: Thirty-one kilometers of mined causeway against a sweep rate of 800 meters per hour: the clearance math says roughly 39 team-hours against a 91-hour scram clock, and the math is the mission.

dataBlock.Mine estimate: 47 charges (confidence MED, 6 days old), sited with an engineer's eye for chokepoints and pylon footings
dataBlock.Sweep rate: 800 meters per hour per engineering vehicle; roughly 39 hours single-team end to end
dataBlock.Two-team option: sweeping from both ends halves the time and requires the Duchy militia's engineers — which requires the Duchy militia's colonel
dataBlock.Mine-kill cost: a transporter kill blocks the single working lane for 3 hours minimum

phases.protocol: Cleared-lane marking: pylon number chalked, sweep-team initials under it, and every kilometer re-walked by a second team before convoy traffic — chalk without initials is treated as unswept. The militia adopted the same convention on day 1; the observer asked for that in writing, and got it.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The difference between swept and safe: what 800 meters per hour buys at night, in brine fog, with refugee traffic shuffling 3 meters from the detector heads.

phases.name: SLOT DISCIPLINE
phases.lead: One convoy per 6-hour slot, single lane. The scram clock pays out 15 slots before H+91; the cooling train needs 3 of them and the food needs 18 more behind it. The schedule is the battlefield — the raids are only weather.

dataBlock.Slot table: 6 hours per slot, 1 convoy per slot, second lane held by refugee counterflow
dataBlock.Stay-behind doctrine: 90-120 minute raids, mine strikes, checkpoint attacks — never decisive engagement, always against the schedule
dataBlock.Refugee rule: 'Mech movement above walking pace scatters the counterflow — casualty roll, observer's incident report, 12-hour militia stand-down
dataBlock.Recovery: the heavy crane reaches a kilometer-12 blockage from the city end in 1 hour, if the refugee lane is opened — a decision with a casualty risk attached

sidebarKernel.kernel: Slots as the campaign's currency: the running count of spent, lost, and remaining, posted at the column head where the drivers can read it too.

phases.name: THE HANDOVER
phases.lead: The last 4 kilometers belong to the militia by law and to Rider 6 by politics: federal escort halts at the city limit marker at causeway kilometer 27, loads transfer under the observer's eye, and the cooling train's final leg rides with troops who answer to a different colonel.

dataBlock.Transfer point: city limit marker, causeway kilometer 27; federal 'Mechs do not pass it for any reason
dataBlock.Breach price: any federal 'Mech across the line suspends the relief authorization 72 hours while every clock keeps running
dataBlock.Final leg: 4 kilometers, Duchy militia escort only, to the station's north intake yard

phases.protocol: Handover form at kilometer 27: transporter crews stay with their loads — escorts change, drivers do not. The militia signs a receipt per load with a copy to the observer unasked; the file that is offered reads better than the file that is demanded. Codeword TURNKEY on the column net means load 3 of 3 is across the line and the federal escort is released to the causeway.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The precedent ledger: each concession to the militia colonel this week becomes Duchy doctrine next week — which ones are worth slots, and which are worth refusing in front of the observer.

assetDetails.detail: Heat-exchanger assemblies on cradle transporters. Load 2 carries the manifold sections that exist nowhere else on {WORLD}; loads 1 and 3 have partial spares at the provincial depot. Whatever order the convoy runs, load 2 never takes the swept lane's worst kilometer first.

Files nightly to 23 assembly members, 9 of whom voted no. Writes what is shown, not what is said — the column's best instrument for surviving Rider 6 is the observer's own file, fed honestly and early.

Staked a career on the H+91 projection and recalculates it every 12 hours as the backup exchangers wear. The figure can move in either direction, and the column hears updates 6 hours stale through militia channels unless a federal liaison sits in the control room — which Rider 6 permits, since a liaison is not a BattleMech.

title: OPERATION FIRST FURROW
skeleton: a lead battalion must hold a drop zone and an intact fuel node for a fixed 50-hour window while a self-spreading peat fire it cannot fully control rewrites the ground daily and the defender spends everything inside the beachhead's lethal first window
inspiration: an airhead seizure that must hold to a fixed link-up hour or doom the main landing — the Pegasus/Orne bridgehead, June 1944
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The task force's main body lands at H+50. Your battalion lands at H+0, and holding the ground until they arrive is the entire job. Objective area: the Sorrel Downs drop zone and the Carsewell fuel works 6 kilometers to the east — a hydrogen cracking plant with 9 storage spheres, the supply hub the whole campaign's ground logistics depend on. Hold both for 50 hours and the campaign for {WORLD} begins on schedule. Lose either one and the main body has to divert to the alternate drop zone, EXLEY, 400 kilometers south; the campaign then starts 9 days late, and your battalion's failure becomes the first thing the after-action review examines. The ground itself is a threat. The Downs are drained peat moor at the end of the dry season, and energy weapons, fires, and engine exhaust all set the peat alight. Smoldering fire fronts spread at 150 to 250 meters per hour with the wind, cut visibility to 100 to 300 meters for days, and burn underground along the old drainage channels — so ground that held a 'Mech on the first day can vent smoke on the second and erupt in flame on the third. This hazard threatens both sides equally. Rules of engagement: no inferno or incendiary weapons within 2 kilometers of the tank farm, because a hit on a storage sphere ends the mission's whole purpose no matter who fired it. Garrison picture, from {NPC:intel-source}, is 14 days old and rated fair: 1 'Mech company at the spaceport 31 kilometers west, 1 more at the capital 300 kilometers north, 1 armor company, 1 infantry regiment with a strong presence in the drainage-channel network, and an aerospace pair at the spaceport airstrip. The spaceport company commander ({NPC:opfor-commander}) is assessed as aggressive and hungry for promotion — and the same report notes he has never once reported a failed attack, which the analysts read two ways: either he never fails, or he hides it when he does. The defenders understand the doctrine as well as you do — a beachhead either dies in its first 50 hours or holds for good — so they will throw everything they have at you inside that window. Expect the works' garrison platoon to start preparing demolition charges the moment they spot your landing burns. Wiring a site that size takes about 16 hours by their doctrine — though that figure comes from captured pre-war {TARGET_FACTION} manuals, not this garrison, so do not bank on it. Your air cover lands at H+8. Until then the sky belongs to the enemy's aerospace pair, and the Downs offer almost no cover.

objectives.primary: Seize and hold the Carsewell fuel works intact and the Sorrel Downs DZ perimeter until main body retro-burn at H+50.
objectives.secondary: Break the spaceport company's combat power as it counterattacks — meet it on the Downs, not among the spheres.
objectives.bonus: Capture the works' administrative records intact; the export ledgers feed the intelligence picture of {TARGET_FACTION} fuel allocation across the district ({NPC:quest-giver} settles such debts in favors).

complications.name: Peat Fire Map
complications.text: Every energy hit and every fire on the dry moor rolls for ignition. Fronts move with the wind, smoke blinds both sides, and the burn travels underground along the drainage cuts to surface where nobody planned. By H+20 the battlefield has terrain that was not on the drop overlay.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Energy weapon misses and burning wrecks: ignition roll on dry peat. Active fronts advance 150-250 meters per hour downwind; smoke zones cap visibility at 100-300 meters; ground over burned-out cuts: collapse check for units above 40 tons. Fires persist 4-10 days.

complications.name: Scatter
complications.text: Drop dispersion puts one lance 6 kilometers off-template at H+0, on the wrong side of the moor, with the enemy aerospace pair hunting exactly this.
complications.mechanicalEffect: 1 lance begins 6 kilometers from the perimeter and must rejoin under air threat. The battalion fights the first 90 minutes understrength by that lance.

complications.name: Their Air, First
complications.text: The {TARGET_FACTION} pair flies from H+0:20 and your cover lands at H+8. Eight hours is a long time to be interesting to two ground-attack pilots with a full magazine and a known target box.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From H+0:35 to H+8:00: one strafing or bombing pass against any element moving in the open, per 30 minutes. Smoke zones and the drainage cuts block targeting; the tank farm's 2-kilometer ROE ring inhibits their ordnance too — they want the spheres intact as much as anyone.

complications.name: The Cut Network
complications.text: The drainage cuts are 3-meter-deep channels netting the whole moor, and the garrison's infantry regiment trained in them. Under smoke, they move battalion-scale forces below line of sight.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Enemy infantry in the cuts: detected only at 200 meters or by dedicated sensor picket. SRM ambush range engagements; perimeter sensor coverage degraded one step while smoke zones are active.

decisionPoints.name: The Works, Hour One
decisionPoints.context: The fuel works sits 6 kilometers east with a garrison platoon and an engineering section that started preparing demolition the moment your retro-burns lit their sky. Sixteen hours of wiring doctrine says the spheres are safe until roughly H+16. Doctrine is a planning figure, not a promise.

options.title: Coup de Main
advantages: The lead lance can be at the works by H+1:10, before any demolition sequence matures
A garrison platoon surprised at hour one surrenders more often than it fights
disadvantages: The lance outruns its support into a built-up site under the ROE ring — if the platoon fights, it is a knife fight among spheres you cannot shoot back into
The DZ perimeter forms understrength while its fastest lance is 6 kilometers east
options.consequence: The works falls intact in the first two hours or becomes a hostage situation with your lance inside the ring — and either way the perimeter meets the H+2:00 recon probe one lance light.

costs.resource: the DZ perimeter forms understrength — its fastest lance 6 kilometers east when the H+2:00 probe arrives
costs.risk: if the platoon fights, a knife fight among spheres the ROE ring forbids shooting back into

options.title: Deliberate Attack at H+20
advantages: Full battalion, proper reconnaissance, the scattered lance recovered, your air cover overhead
Engagement on your terms with the cut network mapped by H+18 patrols
disadvantages: The 16-hour wiring doctrine expires before the attack starts — the assault goes in against a site that is, on paper, ready to blow
20 hours gives {NPC:opfor-commander} time to reinforce the works garrison if he reads your intent
options.consequence: The professional solution, staked entirely on the bet that a garrison commander will not actually destroy the asset he is charged with keeping — a bet the analysts rate as good and cannot prove.

costs.resource: 20 of the 50 holding hours, spent before the first shot at the works
costs.risk: the assault goes in 4 hours past the 16-hour wiring doctrine — against a site that is, on paper, ready to blow

options.title: Bypass and Screen
advantages: The battalion concentrates on the one objective that cannot be wired: the DZ perimeter
A screened works is a works nobody is shooting inside of — the spheres' best protection is a quiet siege
disadvantages: The works stays in enemy hands as a bargaining piece, and the enemy knows what the campaign priced it at
The main body arrives at H+50 to find its fuel node hostage, and the question of whose problem that was has an answer
options.consequence: The perimeter holds at full strength while {NPC:opfor-commander} negotiates the battle around 9 spheres of leverage — the assault succeeds and hands the campaign a standoff it specifically paid your battalion to prevent.

costs.resource: the campaign's priced fuel node, left in enemy hands as 9 spheres of leverage
costs.risk: the main body lands at H+50 to a hostage standoff your battalion was paid to prevent

decisionPoints.name: The Seam
decisionPoints.context: H+9. The counterattack arrives where the planners said it would: the boundary between your battalion and the attached conscript infantry battalion holding the south arc. The conscripts are bending. The reserve lance is the only reserve there is, and the clock shows 41 hours still to hold.

options.title: Refuse the Flank
advantages: Trading ground keeps the battalion intact for the remaining 41 hours
The ground being traded is burning moor — the fires the morning's fight ignited become the new flank guard, and they do not take casualties
disadvantages: The DZ perimeter contracts; drop-supply points and the aid station displace under fire
Ground given on peat is not reliably retaken — the burn map decides, not the staff
options.consequence: The battalion survives the morning at the price of a smaller beachhead, and the main body's landing template at H+50 must be redrawn around terrain that is now on fire.

costs.resource: DZ perimeter footage — drop-supply points and the aid station displace under fire
costs.risk: ground given on burning peat is not reliably retaken; the burn map decides, not the staff

options.title: Commit the Reserve
advantages: A fresh lance at the seam at the moment of crisis is how counterattacks die — the textbook agrees
Holding the original trace keeps the full landing template intact for H+50
disadvantages: The reserve, spent at H+9, does not exist at H+26 when the capital company arrives by airlift
If this attack is the feint, the real one finds a battalion with nothing left in pocket
options.consequence: The seam holds and the beachhead keeps its shape — and for the next 41 hours every alarm on the perimeter is answered by whoever is standing closest, because the pocket is empty.

costs.resource: the only reserve lance, spent at H+9 — the pocket is empty when the capital company arrives at H+26
costs.risk: if this attack is the feint, the real one finds a battalion with nothing left in pocket

options.title: Fire Mission, Danger Close
advantages: The grounded DropShips' naval-grade batteries can erase the penetration in two salvos
Costs no maneuver element — the reserve stays whole for H+26
disadvantages: The seam is 1.8 kilometers from the tank farm: every round is inside the ROE ring, rolling against the spheres
Conscript infantry is decisively engaged in the target box — the fire mission goes through them or waits for a gap that may not come
options.consequence: The counterattack is broken from orbit-grade tubes at the cost of betting the mission's object on dispersion tables — and the conscript battalion's survivors will remember who called it, whichever way the dice land.

costs.resource: the ROE ring's integrity — every round rolls against the spheres at 1.8 kilometers
costs.risk: conscript infantry decisively engaged inside the target box; a sphere hit ends the mission's object regardless of who fired

entries.event: First retro-burn visible from the spaceport. The alarm is your own arrival; the garrison clock and yours start together.
{TARGET_FACTION} aerospace pair scrambles; first strafing pass over the DZ at approximately T+0:35.
Recon probe — 1 light lance and a hover section — tests the perimeter's north arc and withdraws on contact.
Spaceport company plus armor counterattacks the battalion boundary on the south arc.
Capital company arrives by airlift and road march, committed wherever the H+9:00 attack found softness.
Main body retro-burn — if the perimeter and the works still stand.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The DZ perimeter and the Carsewell fuel works intact at H+50, when the main body commits to its final approach. A broken perimeter or burning works at any point before that diverts the landing to EXLEY, 400 kilometers south: the campaign starts 9 days late, the enemy gets 9 days to dig, and the after-action review starts with your battalion's name.

opforSketch.composition: {TARGET_FACTION} garrison: 2 BattleMech companies (Regular, medium-heavy mix, 1 Veteran command lance), 1 armor company, 1 infantry regiment (Green-to-Regular, strongest in the cut network), aerospace pair (Veteran). Generator should produce a counterattack force with armor support for the H+9 attack and infiltration infantry throughout.
opforSketch.behavior: Doctrinal beachhead response: probe, then commit everything inside the 50-hour window — they know the clock as well as you do. Infantry infiltrates under smoke along the cuts; the spaceport company commander presses attacks past their culmination rather than report failure, which is exploitable and dangerous in equal measure.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND WAVE
forks.trigger: Main body lands on schedule at H+50 with works and perimeter intact.
forks.consequence: The campaign opens on schedule and your battalion — blooded, proven, and sitting on the fuel it captured itself — is given the lead role in the drive toward the spaceport. Doing well here just earns the unit a harder job next; that is how the front rewards success.

forks.name: OPERATION SOUTH FORTY
forks.trigger: Perimeter broken or works lost before H+50; main body diverts to EXLEY.
forks.consequence: The battalion fights as a bypassed pocket on the Downs for 9 days — resupply by air drop, peat fires for concealment, the cut network for movement — until the diverted campaign grinds 400 kilometers north to relieve what is left.

forks.name: OPERATION ASH WIND
forks.trigger: DZ held at H+50 but the fuel works destroyed or burned.
forks.consequence: The landing proceeds; the logistics plan does not. Campaign fuel converts to seaborne haul from the coast, and the battalion spends the next phase escorting tanker convoys down roads it was supposed to have made unnecessary — every escort mission a reminder with a schedule attached.

storyElementSeed: A platoon sergeant walks the perimeter at dusk pushing a steel rod into the peat every ten paces, feeling for warmth; where the rod comes up hot, a stake with a cloth strip goes in, and the fighting positions move again without anybody being asked twice.

merc.objectives.primary: Hold the DZ and the fuel works to H+50. The diversion clause in the master contract makes your frontage the single point of failure for 11 other units' payday, and every one of them will read the after-action report with a lawyer.

resourceGates.lackingText: No grounded DropShip batteries on call: the fire mission does not exist, and the seam is held with maneuver elements or not at all.

phases.name: LODGEMENT
phases.lead: From first retro-burn to H+8 the battalion is alone under someone else's sky: one lance 6 kilometers off-template, a fuel works on a 16-hour wiring doctrine, and a perimeter that exists wherever a 'Mech is standing. Every hour of this phase buys the shape of the next 42.

dataBlock.Air: enemy pair flies from H+0:20, first pass near H+0:35; friendly cover lands H+8
dataBlock.Scatter: 1 lance rejoining from 6 kilometers off-template — the battalion fights 90 minutes understrength
dataBlock.Wiring doctrine: 16 hours from first retro-burn sighting to a demolition-ready works (UNCONFIRMED — basis: pre-war {TARGET_FACTION} engineering manuals)
dataBlock.ROE ring: no inferno or incendiary munitions within 2 kilometers of the tank farm; a sphere hit ends the mission's object regardless of who fired

routes.name: Axis COULTER
routes.desc: direct across the open moor to the fuel works, 6.0 kilometers, 22 minutes at lance speed
routes.tradeoff: Fastest path to the works while the wiring is immature; open to the air pair the whole way, and every energy miss rolls peat ignition along your own axis of advance.

routes.name: Axis HARROW
routes.desc: the drainage-cut shoulders, 8.3 kilometers below the cut lips
routes.tradeoff: Masked from air and sensors; the cuts belong to the garrison's infantry regiment, and inside them SRM range is ambush range.

sidebarKernel.kernel: The opfor commander has never reported a failed attack — read it both ways in the same paragraph: what it does to his H+2:00 probe, and to his H+9:00 main effort when the probe's report was flattering.

phases.name: THE COUNTERATTACK
