phases.lead: H+9 to H+26 is the battle the defenders planned: the spaceport company plus armor into the battalion seam, infantry under the smoke in the cuts, and a reserve decision graded twice — once now, once at H+26 when the capital company lands on whatever softness the first attack found.

dataBlock.H+9:00: spaceport company plus armor company at the south-arc boundary with the conscript battalion

title: OPERATION CINDER LEDGER
skeleton: an investor-underwritten assault must take a trade port at a contracted intact-valuation floor before a relief regiment lands, crossing a filter-eating pumice waste where speed is a signature and a venal rail guild may have already sold the line of advance
inspiration: a commercially financed expedition forced to take its prize undamaged on a banker's deadline — the East India Company's seizure of a treaty port, 19th century
situation: {WORLD}, {DISTRICT}, {YEAR}. The objective is {WORLD}'s spaceport and its warehouse arcology, and the key word throughout the contract is intact: 3 merchant-graf houses financed this assault as an investment in the port's future trade value, and the underwriters' representative ({NPC:employer-contact}) travels with task force headquarters carrying a copy of the prospectus and a pen to itemize every bit of damage you do. Your battalion leads. The drop zone is 110 kilometers north of the port — beyond the reach of the garrison's aerospace until your own air cover arrives at H+12 — and between the DZ and the city lies the Cinder Sea: 80 kilometers of pumice barrens, a terrain problem that is really a logistics problem. Pumice grit clogs heat exchangers and air intakes: every vehicle burns 1 filter set per 100 kilometers, 'Mechs run +1 heat in churned-up dust, and any force moving fast throws up a dust plume visible from 20 kilometers away — on the Cinder Sea, moving fast means being seen. There is no water on the crossing; the battalion needs 11 tons a day, hauled forward from the DZ every 18 hours. The battalion's filter stock is 600 sets, and that stock is a countdown: once it runs out, the vehicles stop until the DZ can resupply. Plan the crossing so it never does. Garrison picture, via {NPC:intel-source}, is 8 days old and rated fair: 1 {TARGET_FACTION} 'Mech company, 2 armor companies, and 1 infantry battalion under a commander ({NPC:opfor-commander}) assessed as patient and politically shrewd, in prepared positions at the edge of the arcology, with an aerospace pair operational until H+12. The hardest deadline comes from orbit: a {TARGET_FACTION} relief regiment's JumpShips are inbound, and the transit math gives you 96 hours before that regiment can land wherever it likes and you can no longer stop it. The assault carried 21 days of supply; the plan for after that is to live off the garrison's own captured stocks — the kind of plan that works right up until it becomes a cautionary tale. One asset matters across the whole operation: the salt-rail line running along the Sea's eastern edge, operated by a civilian rail guild whose neutrality is openly for sale — and which has sold to the enemy before. {NPC:fixer} brokers the guild's contracts, and the read on its loyalty is 8 days old and rated low, so trust it with nothing you cannot afford to have sold. The graf houses bought a port, and the {TARGET_FACTION} commander knows exactly what they paid for it. Your route of advance runs between those two facts.

objectives.primary: Capture the spaceport and warehouse arcology at 85 percent or better intact valuation by H+96.
objectives.secondary: Destroy or compel the withdrawal of the garrison battalion without fighting inside the arcology.
objectives.bonus: Capture the garrison's fuel and stores reserve — the task force's sustainment plan past day 21 assumes it.

complications.name: Filter Ledger
complications.text: 600 filter sets, 1 per vehicle per 100 kilometers, consumption doubled in dust storms. The quartermaster's stack of spent cartridges is the truest map of the advance, and it only grows.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track filter sets as a campaign resource. Below 100 sets: vehicle operations curtailed to essential movement. At 0: vehicles immobilized pending DZ resupply, 'Mechs operate alone at +1 heat.

complications.name: Their Air Until H+12
complications.text: The garrison pair flies armed reconnaissance from H+0:25, and on the Cinder Sea every moving element writes its position in the sky behind it. Plume discipline is survival arithmetic until your cover lands.
complications.mechanicalEffect: H+0:25 to H+12:00: elements that moved above half speed in the preceding hour are automatically located; 1 air attack per element per 2 hours available to the OpFor. Stationary or slow elements in broken ground: located only on dedicated search.

complications.name: The Underwriters' Pen
complications.text: The graf houses' representative itemizes warehouse damage in real time against the prospectus, and the task force commander receives the running total with breakfast. Fire missions near the arcology have a price per shell that has nothing to do with ammunition.
complications.mechanicalEffect: All indirect fire and air support within the arcology district requires command release. Each percentage point of intact valuation lost below 85 reduces the operation's political support one step; below 70 percent, the underwriters invoke the diversion clause and the campaign's funding question reopens mid-battle.

complications.name: Dust Storm Season
complications.text: One window in four brings a storm off the Sea: all air grounded, visibility 200 meters, filters burning double. It is the worst movement weather and the best assault cover on the planet, in the same 12-to-24-hour package.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each 48-hour window: 25 percent storm chance. During storm: no air operations either side, visibility 200 meters, filter consumption x2, plume signature negated. Storms end in 12-24 hours.

decisionPoints.name: Crossing the Ledger
decisionPoints.context: Eighty kilometers of pumice between the battalion and the objective, a filter stock that doubles as a countdown, an enemy air pair that owns the sky for the first 12 hours, and a rail guild that will carry anything for anyone who pays. The crossing decides the campaign — and each way across it costs something different: time, filters, or trust.

options.title: Night Road March
advantages: Slow, cold, plume-minimal movement arrives at H+30 with the air threat mostly cheated
Filter consumption stays near book rate — roughly 40 percent of stock spent on arrival
disadvantages: 30 hours of the 96 spent in transit before the first shot at the objective
The garrison watches a deliberate approach develop for more than a day and fortifies accordingly
options.consequence: The battalion arrives intact and on a predictable axis at a prepared position — the engagement opens on time, against an enemy that used your discipline as his planning calendar.

costs.resource: filter sets: roughly 40 percent of the 600-set stock spent on arrival
costs.risk: the garrison watches a deliberate approach develop for 30 of your 96 hours and fortifies accordingly

options.title: Daylight Forced March
advantages: Arrival at H+16 — the garrison gets half the preparation time and the relief clock gets 14 extra hours of margin
Speed may catch the arcology defense incomplete and the stores reserve unevacuated
disadvantages: The plume announces the axis to everyone with eyes, and the air pair gets 2 to 4 clean attack windows during the crossing
Filter consumption near 60 percent of stock; vehicles arrive on the margin of the ledger
options.consequence: The battalion buys 14 hours with airframe damage, burned filters, and a known axis — fast enough to matter, loud enough to be met.

costs.resource: filter sets: roughly 60 percent of the 600-set stock — vehicles arrive on the ledger's margin
costs.risk: the plume hands the garrison air pair 2 to 4 clean attack windows during the crossing

options.title: Buy the Rail Guild
advantages: 1 company plus heavy supplies arrive by rail at H+14, fresh, with filter stock untouched
The guild's rolling stock raises no plume and triggers no air interdiction the {TARGET_FACTION} is willing to pay for politically
disadvantages: The guild's price is 85,000 C-bills plus a neutrality letter, and the guild has sold schedules to the {TARGET_FACTION} before — how it will lean this time is anyone's guess
The force divides: rail element and overland element fight separately if the schedule leaks
options.consequence: The fastest, freshest arrival on the board, riding rolling stock whose operators' last recorded customer was the enemy — the underwriters approve the expense and the intelligence officer files a formal reservation.

costs.resource: a signed neutrality letter the guild can show the {TARGET_FACTION}; the force fights divided if the schedule leaks
costs.risk: the guild's last recorded customer was the enemy — loyalty assessment confidence LOW

decisionPoints.name: The Commander's Offer
decisionPoints.context: H+60. The garrison commander signals under flag: he will withdraw his battalion from the port district with arms and stores, sparing the arcology entirely. The relief regiment lands in 36 hours. The offer is genuine, time-limited, and shaped exactly like a trap that is also a bargain.

options.title: Accept the Withdrawal
advantages: The arcology transfers at 100 percent intact valuation — the prospectus number, the one the underwriters toast
Zero further casualties for the primary objective; the battalion fortifies the port before the relief lands
disadvantages: An intact, supplied {TARGET_FACTION} battalion redeploys to join the relief regiment — you will fight these same men inside 20 days at full strength
The stores reserve walks out the gate with him, and day 21 of the supply plan becomes a fiction
options.consequence: The port is won whole and the war on {WORLD} is extended: the campaign's first battle ends with the enemy's army improved in position and the sustainment plan amputated — the graf houses get their warehouse and the soldiers get the bill.

costs.resource: the garrison's fuel and stores reserve, escorted out the gate — day 21 of the sustainment plan becomes fiction
costs.risk: an intact, supplied {TARGET_FACTION} battalion rejoins the relief regiment — the same men at full strength inside 20 days

options.title: Refuse and Storm
advantages: The garrison is destroyed or captured before the relief lands — the only outcome that simplifies the next 90 days
The stores reserve is taken, not escorted away: the sustainment plan survives
disadvantages: Arcology fighting costs 2 to 4 percent of intact valuation per defended block, and the defense holds 11 blocks
The underwriters' running total arrives at headquarters in real time, with annotations
options.consequence: The military problem is solved at the direct, witnessed, itemized expense of the financial one — and at a block between the first and the eleventh, the exact one unknowable in advance, the political support for the campaign crosses the diversion threshold.

costs.resource: intact valuation: 2 to 4 percent per defended block, with 11 blocks held and the 85 percent floor in the prospectus
costs.risk: the diversion threshold crosses at a block between the first and the eleventh — unknowable in advance, itemized in real time

options.title: Accept, Then Interdict the Stores
advantages: The men walk free under the flag while the materiel — the part the relief regiment actually needs — is taken on the road
Reads, in the operations summary, as a stores seizure rather than a massacre
disadvantages: The {TARGET_FACTION} will classify it as perfidy under flag regardless of the summary's wording, and they will be more right than wrong
No parley will be offered or honored on this front for the remainder of the war — every future garrison fights to the last round
options.consequence: Port intact, stores taken, enemy battalion neutered — the best tactical outcome on the board, purchased with the campaign's honor at a price that compounds: the relief regiment arrives angry, and every city on {WORLD} afterward must be stormed because of what happened on this road.

costs.resource: the campaign's parole credit, classified as perfidy under flag and spent for the rest of the war
costs.risk: no parley offered or honored on this front again — every city on {WORLD} afterward must be stormed

entries.event: Drop plume on the port's watch radar; garrison alert. The alarm is your arrival, and both clocks start.
Garrison aerospace pair up: armed reconnaissance toward the DZ and the Cinder Sea margins.
Garrison recon — hover section and 1 light lance — enters the Sea's southern margin to find the axis.
Your air cover operational; air parity over the Sea from this hour.
Garrison commits: either a forward defense at the Sea's edge or full fortification of the arcology threshold. Intelligence cannot say which, and both are prepared.
{TARGET_FACTION} relief regiment lands at a site of its choosing.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The port in hand by H+96. Past that hour the relief regiment grounds wherever it pleases, and the assault converts to a meeting engagement against a fresh regiment — fought by a battalion down to whatever is left of its 21 days of supply, a filter stock near zero, and an underwriters' representative whose pen has stopped being friendly.

opforSketch.composition: {TARGET_FACTION} garrison: 1 BattleMech company (Regular, Veteran command lance), 2 armor companies, 1 infantry battalion in prepared arcology positions, aerospace pair (Regular) until H+12. Generator should provide dug-in armor at the Sea's edge, infantry-heavy arcology defense, and a commander's reserve held for the counterstroke.
opforSketch.behavior: Patient trade of space for time: raids on water convoys, air interdiction of anything raising a plume, no decisive engagement west of the arcology threshold. {NPC:opfor-commander} knows the port's value to your paymasters to the C-bill and prices every choice accordingly — expect offers, delays, and exactly one counterattack, timed against the relief clock, not yours.

forks.name: OPERATION WAREHOUSE CROWN
forks.trigger: Port and arcology captured at 85 percent or better valuation by H+96.
forks.consequence: The underwriters exercise the development concession and the next assault in the campaign is funded before this one's salvage is sorted. The unit's name appears in the prospectus annex — which in the merchant houses' boardrooms is a credential, a marketing document, and a target, in that order.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG WINTER ACCOUNT
forks.trigger: H+96 passes without the port in hand; relief regiment lands.
forks.consequence: The campaign goes positional on a world that now hosts 2 fresh {TARGET_FACTION} regiments. Withdrawal negotiations begin with the underwriters' lawyers in the room, and the battalion holds a perimeter on the Cinder Sea while the people who funded the assault decide what its survivors are still worth.

forks.name: OPERATION GUILD RATE
forks.trigger: Evidence surfaces that the rail guild sold the battalion's movement schedule to the garrison.
forks.consequence: The approach was watched the whole way; ambush positions along the rail line confirm it. The guild's bridges and rolling stock become a target folder the underwriters' representative refuses to countersign — civilian rail is trade infrastructure, says the prospectus — and the battalion must finish the assault while its line of communication belongs to a vendor of proven flexibility.

storyElementSeed: A supply clerk stacks spent filter cartridges in a pyramid beside the maintenance tent, one per vehicle per hundred kilometers, squaring the edges each evening; the pyramid is the only record of the advance that nobody argues with.

merc.objectives.primary: Take the port at 85-plus percent intact by H+96. The intact-valuation scale in annex C is the pay table; read it before you plan fires, because the employer already has.

resourceGates.lackingText: Below 85,000 C-bills the guild offers terms: half on signature, half advanced from the underwriters' contingency line — which puts {NPC:employer-contact}'s pen on the routing order and the schedule in the prospectus file.

No secured DZ depot: water (11 tons per day) and filter resupply ride the assault echelon itself — every crossing option prices one day slower and the filter ledger starts the campaign already spending.

phases.name: THE CROSSING
phases.lead: Eighty kilometers of pumice between the DZ and the objective, paid for in filters, water, and hours off a 96-hour clock. On the Cinder Sea, moving fast gets you seen and moving slow burns the clock — and the garrison watches whichever choice you make.

routes.name: Route PUMICE
routes.desc: the direct line across the central barrens, 80 kilometers of churned fines
routes.tradeoff: Shortest distance, worst dust: book-rate filter burn, +1 heat in the churn, and a plume visible at 20 kilometers writing the axis in the sky.

routes.name: Route MARGIN
routes.desc: the Sea's eastern edge along the salt-rail embankment, 95 kilometers on firmer ground
routes.tradeoff: Filter burn near two-thirds of book and a thinner plume; every kilometer is observed by a rail guild whose neutrality carries a posted price and a sales history.

phases.name: INVESTMENT
phases.lead: From the Sea's edge to the arcology threshold the assault becomes a siege conducted under a prospectus: the garrison trades space for time and raids the water line; the battalion closes in against a valuation table that prices every fire mission before it lands.

phases.protocol: Fire release inside the arcology district: requests by block number against the prospectus overlay; release authority rests with the task force commander alone; the underwriters' representative logs every release by serial and shell count. Plan 20 minutes from request to splash and zero re-attacks — the overlay is the working ROE, and annex C's pay table is stapled to it.

phases.name: THE PORT
phases.lead: The endgame runs 3 clocks at once: a time-limited withdrawal offer, a relief regiment 36 hours out, and a valuation ticker the underwriters read at breakfast. Whatever is decided is executed inside a warehouse district the campaign is forbidden to break.
